DifficultyDef.label: peaceful
DifficultyDef.description:
Build a community in a sandbox environment. Major direct threats are disabled, but challenges like disease, mental breaks, and mad animals can still occur.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Players who want to learn the game mechanics with minimal pressure. - Players who just want to build. - Players who just want to relax.

DifficultyDef.label: community builder
DifficultyDef.description:
Build a community with a taste of danger. Threats appear, but they're weakened.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Players who are new to this kind of game. - Players who want to build a perfect colony. - Players who want to relax.

DifficultyDef.label: adventure story
DifficultyDef.description:
There's room to grow and thrive, but it's still a dangerous planet.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Experienced strategy gamers on their first game of RimWorld. - Experienced RimWorld players who want some breathing room to pursue funny or weird goals.

DifficultyDef.label: strive to survive
DifficultyDef.description:
Strive to survive on a rough, tough planet. There will be triumph and tragedy.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Experienced players who want a rough story requiring skill to survive.

DifficultyDef.label: blood and dust
DifficultyDef.description:
Face brutal survival challenges. Even if you play well, people will die. You will need to anticipate threats before they arrive, and seek out every advantage.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Experienced players who want to struggle to survive.

DifficultyDef.label: losing is fun
DifficultyDef.description:
This setting is designed to be unfair. Huge threats will crash upon you without mercy until your colony dies. Only choose this setting if you are happy with the drama of struggling and dying.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Experienced players who want to face a brutal, unfair challenge where even great skill may not prevent death. - Lovers of tragedy. - Digital masochists.

DifficultyDef.label: Custom
DifficultyDef.description:
This setting allows you to define your own playstyle in detail.
(*SectionTitle)Recommended for:(/SectionTitle)
- Players who are happy with one of the standard playstyles levels, but want to change a few things. - Players who want to experiment with something different.

ExpansionDef.label: Royalty
ExpansionDef.description:
Fight or ally with the new Shattered Empire faction.
Gain psychic powers through noble right, tribal nature communion, or artifact theft. Strengthen them through meditation, and use them to win battles and socially influence people. Strengthen your psychic power by meditating in grand thronerooms, in nature, before flames, the dead or blank walls.
Complete quests to earn honor and titles, or riches and gear. Host rich nobles, poor refugees, animals, prisoners, and more. Defend crashed shuttles, serve as aerial shock troops, build monuments, defeat enemies, and recruit visitors.
Use the special privileges of nobility to call Imperial troops, shuttles, and orbital strikes.
New mechanoid clusters may deploy on your map. Wear them down with artillery, do sneaky sabotage, or lure enemies into the danger.
Wield persona weapons with unique traits. Use jump packs for tactical flight and shield packs for emergency defense. Wear cataphract armor, locust armor, grenadier armor, and phoenix armor, each with different tools. Install new body implants to augment brains, stomachs, arms, and skin.
Enjoy a new album of music by Alistair Lindsay.
Host and protect the Stellarch and his guards complete the new royal endgame quest.

ExpansionDef.label: Ideology
ExpansionDef.description:
Create your own belief system with fine control over behaviors, preferences, rituals, symbols, and more. Play as pirate nudist cannibals, blind undergrounder mole people, charitable ranching cowboys, machine-obsessed transhumanists, and more.
Assign social roles like leader, moral guide, and specialist to your colonists.
Hold unforgettable rituals: Dance parties, cannibal feasts, burn and smoke circles, skylantern festivals, sacrifices, gladiator duels, blindings, scarifications, funerals, and more.
Connect with Gauranlen trees and command the dryads that live inside them.
Hunt for ancient relics. Explore long-forgotten ruins, hack downed spacedrones, and infiltrate tribal villages. Attract wealthy pilgrims by presenting your relics in reliquaries. Plunder ancient complexes for treasure. Raid temporary encampments. Help beggars in need, or betray them.
Enslave prisoners to perform work or fight for you.
Place many new buildings linked to belief systems, and see the many visual styles of different beliefs.
Use new apparel, tattoos, and hairstyles desired by believers.
Seek transcendence through a machine god in the new archonexus endgame.

ExpansionDef.label: Biotech
ExpansionDef.description:
Raise a family, control mechanoids, and genetically-modify humans.
Build nurseries, play with babies, keep them happy and fed. Babies grow up into children who play, get into trouble, learn, and take lessons. Give the kids a rich childhood, or leave them in a growth vat until they're adults.
Build and control new kinds of mechanoids. Create combat and labor mechanoids and grow your swarm to a fearsome army and workforce.
Manage the pollution produced by your mechanoids. Freeze it, export it, destroy it with high-tech atomizers, or adapt to it.
Call down three new hyper-deadly commander mechanoids and defeat them for their ancient technology.
Genetically-modify your colonists or prisoners. Curate a collection of genes through trade, quest rewards, and surgical extractions. Recombine and implant genes to customize people to their purpose.
Interact with new factions of brutish pig-people, toxin-immune human bioweapons, fur-covered animal-controlling arctic settlers, fire-breathing horned desert imps, psychic-bonding super-mates, and more.
Explore the dark power of the secret blood-drinkers and use it to live forever.

ExpansionDef.label: Anomaly
ExpansionDef.description:
Awaken the monolith and provoke the insane machine-mind. Anomaly is a horror-themed expansion that adds diverse and twisted threats and lets you build containment facilities for dark entities.
Track down an invisible hunter that steals people's souls. Test and interrogate your people to find out who is infested with a mind-controlling parasite. Destroy a fleshmass infestation before it grows over the whole map and consumes everything. Tamper with obelisks that duplicate, mutate, and abduct your colonists. Venture into underground caverns and kill the momma beast below.
Build a grand containment facility for capturing and studying monsters. Use the power of captured creatures against your enemies. Harvest them for resources to craft void-powered weapons, equipment, apparel, and serums.
Fight macabre cultists to stop them from kidnapping your people with their psychic rituals. Use those same rituals for your own purposes and summon the massed dead, rain rage-filled blood, or steal the minds and health of your foes.
Choose your fate in the new endgame as an abyssal void swallows the world.
This expansion includes a new album of music by Alistair Lindsay.

ExpansionDef.label: Odyssey
ExpansionDef.description:
Build your own ship and travel across the planet!
Start small: just a grav engine, a few rooms, thrusters, and enough fuel to lift off. Over time, make it into a home by adding living quarters, labs, workshops, and everything else your mobile colony needs.
Explore new biomes like the fungal glowforests, glacial plains, and toxic scarlands. Search through crashlanded orbital platforms, insect-infested caves, and other dangerous locations for ancient tech to upgrade your ship.
Fly into space. Land on collapsed space stations, ore-rich asteroids, and derelict satellites. Search for treasure, but be prepared for a fight with other orbital scavengers and mechanoid defenses.
Tame, train, and trade cute new animals that can fly and swim. Teach them to dig and forage, nuzzle your colonists, and track down your foes.
Follow maps and rumours to find quests across the planet. Hunt the alpha thrumbo, raid ancient cryptosleep bunkers, mine through asteroids to loot stashes, and more.
Face the mechhive in a new end game. Seize control of the machine mind, or destroy it for good.
Listen to a new album of music by Alistair Lindsay.

li.label: extremely low expectations

li.description: I am above the little people and should be made happy every moment.

li.label: royal expectations
li.description: My majesty... I can hardly believe it myself. A moment's discomfort is below me.

li.label: elite expectations
li.description: I shouldn't have to endure any inconveniences that distract me from my important role.

li.label: supreme expectations
li.description: My importance here is uncontested, so my comfort must be a critical priority for my people.

tips.li: You can dismiss letters and messages by right-clicking on them.
You can hold the shift key to queue orders on your colonists.
You can right-click and drag to reorder colonists on the colonist bar.
You can select the previous or next colonist with the , and . keys.
Many menus allow you to click and drag a setting to 'paint' it over many entries. This even works for things like outfits or food restrictions.
In the work tab's manual priorities mode, 1 is first priority, while 4 is last priority.
Each colonists' mood is displayed in the background of their icon in the colonist bar at the top of the screen.
Shift-clicking the name of a work type in the Work tab changes settings for all colonists at once.
Right-clicking a number in the Work tab using manual priorities will reduce the priority instead of increasing it.
You can hold the alt key to show detailed information about a specific tile.
In a gunfight, always be behind cover! Right-click and drag to have your drafted fighters form a line.
Right-click and drag to have your drafted fighters form a line. Bunched-up targets are easy to hit!
Smoke totally prevents turrets from detecting targets, but people can still shoot with reduced accuracy.
When designing defences, assume enemies will get inside using drop pods or tunnels. Build internal defensive positions.
Foggy or rainy weather reduces the accuracy of ranged weapons.
You can analyze the chance a shot will hit by selecting the shooter and placing the mouse over the target.
Turrets explode when they take a lot of damage. Don't put them too close together, and don't put your people too close to them.
Some animals explode upon death. You can use transport pods to drop animals on enemies. Think about it.
If you need help in a fight, call your allies using the comms console.
Maddened animals will attack any human, including your enemies. You can use this.
EMP bursts will temporarily disable turrets and shields.
EMP bursts instantly break personal shields.
The hunter stealth stat reduces the chance of animal attacks. It is affected by the hunter's animals and shooting skills.
Animals are more likely to attack when harmed from close range. Long-range, slow-firing weapons are safest for hunting.
Entire herds of animals may attack you when you try to hunt them. Accept the risk before hunting, or choose weaker prey.
If you hunt boomrats and boomalopes when it's raining, their deaths won't cause forest fires.
Carefully-slaughtered animals yield more meat and leather than those who were killed violently.
Place the caravan hitching spot where you want your caravans to form up. It's usually best to place it near your storage areas.
During encounters away from home, you can place a caravan hitching spot to keep your animals from wandering.
Caravans move faster if they include rideable animals like horses, donkeys and dromedaries.
Smaller caravans get attacked less often because they're less visible.
Before forming a caravan, collect the items you want to send in a stockpile near your caravan hitching spot. This will make packing much faster.
If you have untrained animals in your caravan, you can split them into a separate caravan before attacking an enemy, to keep them out of the fight.
Don't forget to pack medicine on your caravans.
RimWorld is a story generator, not a skill test. A ruined colony is a dramatic tragedy, not a failure.
Some colonists are worse than useless. Bad allies are part of the challenge.
If you can't defend against a threat, make a caravan and run. You may lose your home, but your story can continue.
When you have more wealth, more powerful enemies attack. If you want the challenge to scale with time instead, select 'Wealth-independent progress mode' in the storyteller settings.
Avoid using stone for doors. They open very slowly, which wastes your colonists' time.
Put chairs in front of workbenches so workers can sit comfortably while working.
Mechanical structures break down and require replacement components. Don't build things you don't need.
Be careful what you construct on bridges. Bridges collapse easily under explosions, and your buildings will go with them.
Clean rooms increase research speed, improve medical outcomes, and reduce food poisoning. Sterile tiles make rooms extra-clean.
Building your whole colony in one structure saves resources, but also makes it difficult to contain fires.
Terrain affects movement speed. Build floors to help your colonists get around quicker.
Different terrain has different inherent cleanliness levels. Tiles are inherently clean; dirt is inherently dirty.
Some floor types are faster to clean than others. It takes much longer to clean carpet compared to metal tile.
You can give prisoners as gifts. Giving a prisoner back to their own faction will be highly appreciated.
You can request specific types of trade caravans using the comms console.
You can use transport pods to send gifts directly to other factions' bases - even your enemies. This improves faction relations.
Keeping prisoners together saves space. However, prisoners kept together will try to break out together.
Enemy faction bases are very well-defended. You don't need to attack them - but be well-prepared if you choose to try.
Cute tame animals will nuzzle your colonists, improving their mood.
Assign your herbivorous animals to areas with lots of grass. They'll eat the grass and spare you the need to feed them.
If someone has a serious infection in a limb, you can remove the limb to save their life.
Sloshing through water makes people unhappy. Build a bridge when you can.
Luciferium can heal scars - even those on the eye or brain. It is, however, a permanent commitment.
Work and movement speed are affected by lighting. Everything is slower in the dark.
Deep underground caverns have a naturally stable temperature, even if it's very hot or cold outside.
Mountain bases are easy to defend. The downside is that people go crazy spending too long underground. And giant insects.
Prisoners will join much quicker and attempt fewer breakouts when they're in a good mood.
You can have multiple researchers working simultaneously at multiple research tables.
Geysers heat up rooms if enclosed. This can be dangerous, or useful.
Explosions extinguish fires in their blast radius. This makes artillery shells useful for stopping fires when there is no other choice.
Even serious setbacks don't mean the game has to end. Try playing out a lost battle - often the best stories come from the darkest situations.
Keep weapon stockpiles away from your prisons. Prison breaks are much more dangerous with guns and explosives.
When taming animals, make sure you have enough food of the correct type to feed them.
Dropping a stone or slag chunk in a doorway will force it open, leaving you vulnerable to hostile wildlife and raiders.
Clean labs with sterile tile give research speed bonuses.
You can change storyteller and playstyle at any time through the options menu.
The more factions you are allied with, the more random traders and military aid you will receive.
You can use drug policies to have your fighters carry combat drugs like go-juice. A quick dose at the start of combat can win the battle.
Set schedules with long stretches of one activity to minimize travel time.
Straw matting ignores filth. Use it as the floor for your barn.
Some animals produce a lot of filth. Keep your elephants and cattle outside.
Predators won't hunt animals which are on the other side of fences or barricades.
It's never game over. If everyone is dead or gone, you can create new wanderers to take over the remains of your colony.
Store books in bookcases. This increases the beauty of a room, makes nearby research benches faster, and increases the XP and recreation gained from reading.
Want a newly crafted item to be taken to a specific shelf? Once a shelf is named or linked with other shelves, it will appear as a hauling destination in the bill's “Details...” window.
You can change to a 12 hour clock, or change Celsius temperatures to Fahrenheit, in the options menu.
When targeting a colonist with an ability or item, you can also target their portrait in the top colonist bar.
Some buildings are more efficient if they're in a dedicated room. Workbenches in their own room make a workshop. Research benches in their own room make a laboratory.
You can rename bills in the bill details dialog.
Friendly fire can't happen if the shooter is close to their ally. You can safely put melee colonists in front of gun-wielding colonists.
Right-click on certain buttons in the orders menu for additional options. For example, you can forbid all items on a map or cancel all hunting jobs.
Hold the shift key while scrolling the map to scroll faster.
Shelves aren't just for show. They increase your storage capacity by holding multiple items on the same spot.
Mechanoids have some psychic sensitivity. Use a psychic lance on one to turn a fight.
Most colonists hate eating insect meat. Turn it into chemfuel using a biofuel refinery.
Pressing Z will let you search the map for items, creatures, buildings, and more. You can search the world map too.

NeedDef.label: mood
NeedDef.description: Mood represents how happy or stressed someone is. If mood gets too low, the person may suffer a mental break. Depending on how low their mood is, someone who has a mental break may have a minor breaks like hiding in their room for a day, or a major break like going on a murder spree.

NeedDef.label: food
NeedDef.description: Food is the amount of nutrition a creature has consumed recently. If it is at zero, a creature will become increasingly malnourished and eventually die.

NeedDef.label: sleep
NeedDef.description: Sleep is how much time a creature has spent sleeping recently. If it is at zero, a creature will eventually fall asleep on the spot.

NeedDef.label: recreation
NeedDef.description: Recreation is the need to have fun. Repeating the same kind of activity makes it less fun, so variety is necessary.

NeedDef.label: beauty
NeedDef.description: Beauty reflects how visually pleasing a person has found their surroundings recently. Beautiful things like art improve beauty when viewed, while ugly things like filth and rough stone surfaces reduce it.

NeedDef.label: comfort
NeedDef.description: Comfort is gained by sitting in or sleeping on comfortable furniture. It is acquired while laying in bed, sitting in a chair while working, or other times.

NeedDef.label: outdoors
NeedDef.description: Outdoors expresses the need not to be cooped up inside. It is harmed by long periods inside, especially underground. It improves when someone spends time under the sky, especially outdoors. It's not about the size of the rooms, but the need to be outside from time to time. Lack of outdoors time is a significant challenge for people who dwell in underground bases.

NeedDef.label: indoors
NeedDef.description: Indoors expresses the need to feel safe within walls and under a roof. It improves when someone spends time inside.

NeedDef.label: chemical
NeedDef.description: Chemical expresses the desire to ingest drugs. When above a certain level it will create good mood, but when below a certain level it will create increasingly bad mood.

questDescription->A friendly AI from your past named (*Name)Charlon Whitestone(/Name) has sent you a message! 
He reveals that he has a starship hidden on this planet, and sends you its world coordinates. 
The starship is in deep hibernation mode. You'll have to start it up when you arrive, then defend it from raiders trying to steal it until the startup sequence completes. It will be a long, difficult series of battles. 
If you can get the ship off the ground, (*Name)Charlon Whitestone(/Name) will take you off this rimworld, to the stars.

RecipeDef.label: smelt metal from slag
RecipeDef.description: Use heat and strong electromagnets to extract useful metal from slag chunks.

RecipeDef.label: smelt weapon
RecipeDef.description: Use heat and strong electromagnets to break down weapons into useful resources.

RecipeDef.label: smelt apparel
RecipeDef.description: Use heat and strong electromagnets to break down metallic apparel like armor into useful resources.

RecipeDef.label: destroy weapon
RecipeDef.description: Use heat to destroy unwanted weapons. This process is faster than smelting, and works on non-smeltable items, but yields no resources.

RecipeDef.label: destroy apparel
RecipeDef.description: Use heat to destroy unwanted apparel. This process is faster than smelting, and works on non-smeltable items, but yields no resources.

RecipeDef.label: smelt or destroy thing
RecipeDef.description: Use heat and strong electromagnets to break down metallic things like weapons and armor into useful resources, or destroy them if they are not smeltable.

RecipeDef.label: make chemfuel from wood
RecipeDef.description: Make a batch of chemfuel by extracting and condensing wood gas from logs.

RecipeDef.label: make chemfuel from organics
RecipeDef.description: Make a batch of chemfuel by extracting biofuel from organic feedstocks.

RecipeDef.label: make component
RecipeDef.description: Make a component.

RecipeDef.label: make advanced component
RecipeDef.description: Make an advanced component.

RecipeDef.label: make patchleather
RecipeDef.description: Combine various types of leather to create weak patchleather.

RecipeDef.label: anesthetize
RecipeDef.description: Render a creature unconscious by administering general anesthetic.

RecipeDef.label: euthanize by cut
RecipeDef.description: Euthanize a creature by cutting.

RecipeDef.label: remove part
RecipeDef.description: Remove a body part.

{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed catastrophically while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}).
{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed in a ridiculous way while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}).
{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}), leaving {PATIENT_objective} sterile.
{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}), leaving {PATIENT_objective} sterile.
{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed in a minor way while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}).
{SURGEON_labelShort} has failed in a minor way while operating on {PATIENT_labelShort} ({RECIPE_label}).

ResearchProjectDef.label: psychoid brewing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Prepare psychoid leaves into a mildly euphoria-inducing and addictive tea at the campfire or cooking stove.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->joined a short-lived psychoid commune on a cult world
subject_story->experimented with psychoid to help traumatized soldiers
subject_story->legalized psychoid for mass production across several coreworlds, when [ANYPAWN_pronoun] had the power to do so

ResearchProjectDef.label: tree sowing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Sow the local biome's natural trees in your fields.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->propagated trees across a long-dead planetoid, trying to bring life back
subject_story->published a paper about maintaining natural ecosystems
subject_story->worked in a tree nursery on an animal world

ResearchProjectDef.label: beer brewing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a brewery and fermenting vats to transform hops into tasty, tasty beer.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->brewed a unique stout that became famous across the system
subject_story->retired to run a public house on an animal world

ResearchProjectDef.label: complex furniture
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build complex furniture like beds, end tables, dining chairs, armchairs, dressers, tool cabinets, billiards tables, and poker tables, vents, sarcophagi, and more.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->studied woodcarving under a master carpenter
subject_story->built a town of log-cabins singlehandedly
subject_story->established a factory, selling high-quality furniture to passing traders

ResearchProjectDef.label: passive cooler
ResearchProjectDef.description: Make passive coolers, to cool indoor spaces without using electricity.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->moved to a sweltering tropical world and developed unique techniques for staying cool
subject_story->researched primitive techniques for cooling areas in the comfort of a coreworld's libraries
subject_story->noticed, on the shores of an oceanic planet, that it was cooler where the sea spray settled

ResearchProjectDef.label: stonecutting
ResearchProjectDef.description: Cut rock chunks into stone blocks for use in construction. Build beautiful stone tile floors or ugly concrete walkways.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was the first in a line of temple designers, all sharing the same name
subject_story->developed unique techniques for cutting the hardest rock with basic tools
subject_story->tiled the entirety of the viceroy's palace on a medieval world

ResearchProjectDef.label: complex clothing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Tailor complicated garments like pants, dusters, and cowboy hats.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->tailored hard-wearing clothes for urbworld cityfolk
subject_story->would relax by sewing and telling stories to the village children
subject_story->learned to craft clothing to be worn at [ANYPAWN_possessive] troupe's grand performances

ResearchProjectDef.label: drug production
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a drug lab for basic drug synthesis. Further research is required to make specific drugs.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->worked in an asteroid lab on the edge of populated space
subject_story->learned how to craft drugs from recycled chemicals, leading to many years spent in prison
subject_story->worked as a chemist, but slipped into peddling illegal drugs on the side

ResearchProjectDef.label: cocoa
ResearchProjectDef.description: Sow cocoa trees to create your own delicious chocolate. Eating chocolate fulfills the need for recreation and it's a valuable trade good too.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->became obsessed with chocolate and had to be restrained
subject_story->studied the fermentation process of cocoa for a thesis
subject_story->set up the best chocolate shop in the sector

ResearchProjectDef.label: devilstrand
ResearchProjectDef.description: Plant devilstrand, a slow-growing mushroom that yields an exceptionally tough, heat-resistant plant fiber.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->used devilstrand as a natural firebreak
subject_story->established the techniques for cultivating devilstrand easily
subject_story->became obsessed with mushrooms and became the self-declared Princess of [ANYPAWN_possessive] kingdom

ResearchProjectDef.label: carpet-making
ResearchProjectDef.description: Weave beautiful carpets from cloth.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->learned to weave carpets from hair, for a distant Emperor
subject_story->left behind an unparalleled collection of carpets and tapestries
subject_story->settled on a medieval moon, where the carpetweaving craft was truly appreciated

ResearchProjectDef.label: pemmican
ResearchProjectDef.description: Make pemmican, a preserved mixture of meat and plant matter that doesn't go bad for a long time. Great for traveling.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->mastered pemmican production during a long pilgrimage to the planet's Spire
subject_story->survived solely on pemmican when a passenger liner crashed on a glassworld
subject_story->taught pemmican production to feral tribes

ResearchProjectDef.label: smithing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build smithies for crafting metal weapons like knives, gladii, and maces. Work metal into clean, beautiful floor tiles.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->settled in a medieval hamlet and mastered simple metal crafting
subject_story->built glitterworld smithies for the Renaissance reenactment guilds

ResearchProjectDef.label: recurve bow
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build the recurve bow, an effective and inexpensive ranged weapon.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->tracked a rabid boomalope for four days before killing it with a single arrow
subject_story->settled near a yew forest to secure the perfect materials for bows
subject_story->raised the colony children as hunter-gatherers, with every one a master archer

ResearchProjectDef.label: psychite refining
ResearchProjectDef.description: Refine psychoid leaves into flake and yayo, different forms of the euphoric psychite drug.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->used [ANYPAWN_possessive] university job as cover for [ANYPAWN_possessive] drug-dealing
subject_story->started a commune where low-dose flake was mixed into the food
subject_story->campaigned for the legalisation of yayo on a nearby urbworld

ResearchProjectDef.label: wake-up production
ResearchProjectDef.description: Synthesize wake-up, a work performance-enhancing drug which replaces the need for sleep.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->tried to overcome caffeine addiction by taking wake-up
subject_story->treated narcoleptics and sleepwalkers with carefully timed wake-up doses
subject_story->moved everyone to the dark side of an asteroid and used wake-up to maintain their biorhythms

ResearchProjectDef.label: go-juice production
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce go-juice, a synthetic combat-performance-enhancing drug which improves shooting, melee, and movement ability, and dulls pain.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was expelled for taking go-juice during team sports matches
subject_story->found go-juice massively increased productivity in mines and lumberyards
subject_story->never went on a mission without go-juice or juggernaut in a pocket

ResearchProjectDef.label: penoxycyline production
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce penoxycyline, a disease prevention drug which blocks plague, malaria, and more before they start.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->lectured to the United Planets about preventative medicine
subject_story->was driven out of Dawn Falls as a quack, for selling a medicine that "doesn't do anything"
subject_story->prevented an outbreak of malaria from spreading through careful penoxycyline dosage

ResearchProjectDef.label: long blades
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft longswords and spears.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->rode with the Betaduke's Fifth Light Cavalry as they conquered the sector
subject_story->was enslaved as a weaponsmith beneath the arena on an iron age planet
subject_story->trained the hoplites on a warworld to use their weapons' reach

ResearchProjectDef.label: plate armor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Smith suits of plate armor from metal or wood. This heavy armor noticeably slows movement, but protects very effectively.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->crafted armor from scrap, when the authorities surrounded [ANYPAWN_possessive] family's shack
subject_story->became known as the Green Smith, when moss grew on the wooden armor
subject_story->started the first armorworker's collective on an urbworld

ResearchProjectDef.label: greatbow
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft greatbows for killing enemies at great range.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->fired an arrow right through the iron helmet of a feudal king
subject_story->hunted muffalos for their fur on a feral world
subject_story->lived alone in the greenwood, a hail of arrows greeting anyone who approached within a mile of its edge

ResearchProjectDef.label: electricity
ResearchProjectDef.description: Harness the power of electricity for a hundred different tasks.
ResearchProjectDef.discoveredLetterText: Your colony has harnessed the power which outsiders call "electricity". It has the potential to transform every aspect of your people's way of life.\n\nYou have now unlocked the Power tab in the Architect menu from which you may build electric generators, power conduits, and other mechanisms to control this new force. The Power tab also displays the electric grid which connects electric generators and appliances.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was struck by lighting and became determined to harness it
subject_story->created the first generator and lightbulb on a medieval world
subject_story->was executed on a feudal world for the blasphemy of creating light

ResearchProjectDef.label: battery
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build batteries for storing electricity.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->discovered that an acid lake on the leaden shores of a deathworld worked as a natural battery
subject_story->was in charge of maintaining the life support if the colony lost power
subject_story->worked in the scrapworlds, repairing machines and batteries

ResearchProjectDef.label: biofuel refining
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build biofuel refineries to make chemfuel from biological matter like wood or foodstuffs.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was trapped when a generation ship lost power. [ANYPAWN_pronoun] used [ANYPAWN_possessive] knowledge of refining to turn human remains into biofuel and restart the engines
subject_story->used automated biorefineries to begin the long terraforming process on an iceworld
subject_story->started a distillery to make moonshine but, realizing it was undrinkable, sold it as chemfuel instead

ResearchProjectDef.label: watermill generator
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build watermill generators on rivers to generate a steady supply of power.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->watched twigs and leaves get pulled downstream and envisioned the power there
subject_story->hooked cabling up to an ancient flour mill on a feudalworld
subject_story->beached a paddle steamer on a ruinworld's shores and converted it into a watermill

ResearchProjectDef.label: nutrient paste
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build nutrient paste dispensers which efficiently produce edible meals from raw nutritive feedstocks, while requiring no labor at all.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->worked in a factory canteen and devised nutrient paste as a way to avoid all labor
subject_story->lost [ANYPAWN_possessive] taste of smell to disease, so devised a cheap, flavorless nutrient paste
subject_story->advocated for the recycling of all organic matter into nutrient paste, even corpses

ResearchProjectDef.label: solar panel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build solar panels for electricity generation.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->studied ways of maximizing the percentage of solar energy captured
subject_story->left on a sundiver to see a fly-by of a star's photosphere

ResearchProjectDef.label: air conditioning
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build coolers to make people comfortable in hot weather, or to construct freezers for storing perishable goods.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->visited the hottest town on the planet
subject_story->worked at the ice caps, in an interstellar warehouse kept near to absolute zero
subject_story->learned all about air conditioning and freezers, then returned home

ResearchProjectDef.label: autodoor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build autodoors which automatically open when someone approaches, without slowing anyone down.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was recruited by a robotics security firm, opening the door to a career as an automation tester
subject_story->worked very hard to ensure the doors made a satisfying 'hiss' when they opened or closed

ResearchProjectDef.label: hydroponics
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build hydroponics basins to rapidly grow crops indoors regardless of the terrain or weather outside.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->joined a generation ship crew as their crop specialist
subject_story->established a hydroponics facility to feed the hungry
subject_story->traveled around, teaching artificial plant growth to new colonists

ResearchProjectDef.label: tube television
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce tube televisions for recreational watching.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->designed a faux-retro television set that could pick up interstellar signals
subject_story->moved into broadcasting, producing programmes just for the archaic tube televisions
subject_story->ensured that everyone knew the dangers of cathode ray tubes

ResearchProjectDef.label: packaged survival meal
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce packaged survival meals which never go bad. Great for traveling.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story-> knew, when disaster struck, there were enough packaged meals to survive until rescuers arrived
subject_story->established a social kitchen, which donated survival meals to all outgoing vessels
subject_story->discovered survival meals in the mountains that were hundreds of years old

ResearchProjectDef.label: firefoam
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct firefoam poppers, automatic fire-safety devices which spread fire-retardant foam in response to encroaching flames.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->headed up an agency promulgating fire safety to the whole population
subject_story->was saved by the poppers when an oil fire spiraled out of control

ResearchProjectDef.label: IEDs
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build improvised traps from any kind of mortar shell.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->disarmed the leftover shells of the war, sending them onto the new frontline as mines
subject_story->came under mortar fire, only surviving by crafting traps from the enemy's many dud shells
subject_story->advocated for the rights of small settlements, where unexploded munitions were a constant peril

ResearchProjectDef.label: geothermal power
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build geothermal power plants on top of steam geysers, for uninterrupted power.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->studied steam power and established geothermal plants throughout the region
subject_story->tapped the power of a dormant volcano to power the local grid
subject_story->argued with the local population who wanted to preserve the scenic geysers, not use them for power

ResearchProjectDef.label: sterile materials
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct sterile tiles to make cleanrooms for safer and more effective medical treatment, research, and cooking.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->prevented many deaths by insisting on effective, consistent sterilization of all equipment
subject_story->started a kibble kitchen which, uniquely for the system, was known to be free of food poisoning
subject_story->established a decorative tile factory, with a sideline in medical equipment and sterile tiles

ResearchProjectDef.label: advanced lights
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build powerful outdoors lights. Additionally, customize the color of electric lights and reduce their power consumption by half. This does not affect sun lamps.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->installed floodlights all around the prison world's many security perimeters
subject_story->made sure that the planet's dark side was well-lit
subject_story->moved into running concerts for interstellar troubadours, specializing in controlling the ship's massive lighting rigs

ResearchProjectDef.label: machining
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build machining tables to craft guns, grenades, flak armor, and to shred dead mechanoids for resources.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->gathered the remains of dead mechanoids and shredded them for resources
subject_story->quietly built an arsenal of self-made weapons in the basement of a suburban home
subject_story->built machining tables for many gunsmiths, despite being a pacifist

ResearchProjectDef.label: smokepop packs
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build smokepop packs which allow the wearer to deploy a defensive smokescreen.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->worked as a hauler for bands, using smokepops for special effects
subject_story->established a defensive smokepop perimeter around the local towns, to keep the wildlife back
subject_story->used smokepop packs to train new firefighters, without the peril of actual fire

ResearchProjectDef.label: prosthetics
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build inexpensive prosthetic body parts to replace lost limbs. Requires a skilled doctor to attach.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->had a limb replaced with a prosthetic, to show how easy it was
subject_story->began crafting bespoke fake limbs for the many war veterans in the area

ResearchProjectDef.label: gunsmithing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft simple manually-operated guns like revolvers, pump shotguns, bolt-action rifles, and incendiary launchers.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->built a unique 12-shot revolver and won shoot-out after shoot-out
subject_story->specialized in simple gunsmithing, providing shotguns and rifles for hunters
subject_story->set up as a gunsmith, achieving fame across the sector

ResearchProjectDef.label: flak armor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft clothing with metal armor sewn in to resist bullets and explosions. This weighty armor slows movement slightly.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->supplied flak armor to the militias that ran the cities
subject_story->learned to sew metal plates into clothing, to protect kin from the roving gangs
subject_story->survived a rifle bullet thanks to the metal plate sewn into the breast pocket

ResearchProjectDef.label: mortars
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build mortars which can lob shells long distances - even over walls.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was instrumental in the glasshouse siege that overthrew the town council
subject_story->developed a collapsible, lightweight mortar tube for the local police
subject_story->demolished the many derelict buildings from a distance, with explosive shells

ResearchProjectDef.label: blowback operation
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft low-power blowback-operated guns like autopistols and machine pistols.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->utilized machine pistols in the trench fighting that overtook the planet
subject_story->sold low-powered autopistols to law enforcement in the orbitals
subject_story->crafted blowback-operated guns for near-sighted conscripts

ResearchProjectDef.label: gas operation
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft high-power guns like chain shotguns, LMGs, and heavy SMGs.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->equipped the special weapons squads of the tyrant's guard with light machine guns
subject_story->supplied several planetary armies with heavy firearms
subject_story->designed new types of high-power gun, still known today

ResearchProjectDef.label: gun turrets
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce simple automated gun turrets.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->worked on AI routines, to enable gun turrets to identify friends and foes
subject_story->designed a modular gun turret holster, capable of taking any weapon type
subject_story->disabled the enemy's turrets remotely, before leading the charge

ResearchProjectDef.label: foam turret
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce a turret which can be activated to spray fire-extinguishing foam.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->redesigned gun turrets to put out fires, not create them
subject_story->incorporated heat sensors and foam ejectors into a standard turret chassis
subject_story->was praised after installing cheap foam turrets in public areas and saving many lives

ResearchProjectDef.label: microelectronics
ResearchProjectDef.description: Work with complex microelectronics. This unlocks the hi-tech research bench and comms console.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->moved into the development of microelectronics
subject_story->constructed the first of many research bench variants
subject_story->moved from town to town, praising the virtues of pure research

ResearchProjectDef.label: flatscreen television
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce high-resolution flatscreen televisions for greater enjoyment.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->experimented with removing tubes from televisions
subject_story->agitated for galaxy-wide, high-resolution broadcasts of [tv_content]
subject_story->became a television executive, in charge of [tv_content]

ResearchProjectDef.label: moisture pump
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct moisture pumps, which very slowly normalize the moisture in the ground around them. They can turn wet ground dry and convert soft sand into normal sand.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->studied the ancient windmill moisture pumps of Earth
subject_story->drained the great swamps that bred disease
subject_story->tried to drain the seas, foolishly

ResearchProjectDef.label: hospital bed
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct hospital beds which improve medical outcomes.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->oversaw a revolution in the standards of medical care
subject_story->constructed the first of the system's public hospitals
subject_story->focused on profit, selling [ANYPAWN_pronoun] superior medical suites to the wealthy

ResearchProjectDef.label: deep drilling
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build deep drills for extracting resources from underground. You'll need a ground-penetrating scanner to find the resources.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->moved in with a dirtmole-led corp, studying its deepest excavations
subject_story->drilled down to the ice cap's root to discover the world's extinct prehuman biome
subject_story->became wealthy from the resources dug out of the world's core

ResearchProjectDef.label: ground-penetrating scanner
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build ground-penetrating scanners that can detect drillable resources under the surface. Requires an advanced component to construct.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->discovered the bones of ancient giants, far below the planet's surface
subject_story->stumbled across a rich gold seam whilst scanning for tin and became fabulously wealthy
subject_story->scanned the ground for ancient minefields, to protect the people

ResearchProjectDef.label: transport pod
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct launchable transport pods that you can use to send people and supplies long distances across the planet's surface. Can be used for raiding, travel, sending gifts, and more.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->landed a pod in the middle of a feral tribe and barely escaped alive
subject_story->spent a fortune sending a transport pod to the object of [ANYPAWN_possessive] affection, carrying a single wedding ring
subject_story->staved off famine through judicious pod deployment

ResearchProjectDef.label: medicine production
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce standard industrial-tech medicine by combining herbal medicine, neutroamine, and cloth.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->researched urbworld medicine, aiming to distribute the knowledge more widely
subject_story->was puzzled by the origins of neutroamine and determined to find out more
subject_story->seized the resources of a drug-dealer and produced useful medicines instead

ResearchProjectDef.label: long-range mineral scanner
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct long-range mineral scanners your researchers can use to detect precious minerals across the planet. Can be tuned to find a specific mineral. Requires advanced components to construct.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->built so many scanners that the planet's entire geology was revealed
subject_story->discovered with a scanner what the other settlements were mining and made huge profits through trading
subject_story->mined out the entirety of the planet's jade for religious effigies

ResearchProjectDef.label: shields
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build wearable shield gear. Shields use momentum-repulsion technology to prevent projectiles from traversing the field boundary.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->survived an assassination attempt, thanks to a prototype shield
subject_story->hustled at billiards, using a hidden momentum repeller
subject_story->killed an enemy by advancing a blade slowly enough to bypass their shield

ResearchProjectDef.label: precision rifling
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft precisely-machined guns like assault rifles and sniper rifles.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->improved the tolerances of a foundry's processes, enabling the production of quality rifling
subject_story->was hunted by neanderthals but constructed a sniper rifle to safely kill their leader
subject_story->became briefly famous for shooting an ambrosia fruit out of the overlord's hand

ResearchProjectDef.label: autocannon turret
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce the heavy autocannon turret.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->held off a cultist assault alone, hiding behind a wall of turrets
subject_story->was hired to establish a defensive perimeter of sandbags and turrets for the locals
subject_story->built turret after turret, never asking who was buying them

ResearchProjectDef.label: multibarrel weapons
ResearchProjectDef.description: Assemble miniguns.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->constructed a unique portable minigun, which was the only thing found after the squad's disappearance
subject_story->designed massive hoppers to ensure the minigun ammo didn't run out
subject_story->built guns explicitly to kill every last person in a room

ResearchProjectDef.label: multi-analyzer
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build multi-analyzers which increase research speed and allow higher-level research projects.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->unlocked the trans-spectrum secrets of the universe

ResearchProjectDef.label: vitals monitor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build vitals monitors which improve medical outcomes when placed next to hospital beds.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->struggled in an overcrowded hospital and vowed to work for change
subject_story->nursed a glassworld survivor back to health
subject_story->monitored the isolation ward remotely, sending mechanoids in for treatments

ResearchProjectDef.label: fabrication
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build fabrication benches, capable of high-tech projects ranging from component assembly to power armor construction.
ResearchProjectDef.discoveredLetterText:
You now have the technology to build a fabrication bench - but it also requires some advanced components to get started. You can collect advanced components several ways:

 -All outlander settlements sell advanced components. Send a caravan to buy some.
 -Some visiting traders sell advanced components. Invite or wait for them.
 -Some quests are rewarded with advanced components.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->spent many years crafting advanced components, to make fabrication benches to make more advanced components
subject_story->traded everything to build a single fabrication bench
subject_story->constructed technological marvels which the feral villagers worshipped as magical

ResearchProjectDef.label: advanced fabrication
ResearchProjectDef.description: Fabricate advanced components from standard components and other materials.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->traded advanced components to desperate rimworlders
subject_story->learned the secrets of fabricating advanced components and died without revealing them
subject_story->balked at the extreme cost of crafting advanced components and chose a simpler lifestyle

ResearchProjectDef.label: cryptosleep casket
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct cryptosleep caskets, which can put living beings in a state of indefinite suspended animation.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->intended to test a prototype cryptosleep casket and woke a generation later, alone
subject_story->sentenced the system's worst criminal to indefinite cryptosleep rather than death
subject_story->used a cryptosleep capsule to suspend the terminally ill, so they could see their children once they'd grown up

ResearchProjectDef.label: recon armor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Craft recon armor, a light powered armor suit used by scout troops who need protection on the move. Note that these also require advanced components.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->led the rebel scouts against the Imperial forces, until captured
subject_story->crafted powered armor light and resilient enough for the hammer-users to close with the enemy
subject_story->intended recon armor more for hunters than soldiers. It sold well, regardless

ResearchProjectDef.label: marine armor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build marine armor, a general-use powered armor suit used by high-tech shock troops. Note that these also require advanced components.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->was employed by the shock troops to maintain their armor
subject_story->tested the armor by walking, unarmed, through a hostile feral village without receiving a scratch
subject_story->intended the armor as protection against the planet's hostile weather, but it worked well against the pirates too

ResearchProjectDef.label: pulse-charged munitions
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build weapons which fire pulse-charged munitions for extra damage. Note that these also require advanced components.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->studied glitterworld monorails and modified the tech for weapons
subject_story->killed a mechanical crawler by kiting it with a charge lance
subject_story->learned how to imbue rifle ammunition with retained charge, heavily increasing its lethality

ResearchProjectDef.label: bionic replacements
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build high-tech bionic body parts to replace lost limbs and eyes. Requires a skilled doctor to attach.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->worked primarily with disfigured soldiers, crafting bespoke bionic facial elements so they could return to their loved ones
subject_story->studied slowed vids of human motion to better craft bionic prosthetics
subject_story->was volunteered to have the various prototype bionics implanted, ending up as more machine than man

ResearchProjectDef.label: uranium slug turret
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce the armor-penetrating uranium slug turret. It fires uranium slugs which tear through plasteel like paper, but it's less effective at close range.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->led the clean-up after the war, collecting spent radioactive uranium slugs from the front line
subject_story->saw a turret shoot straight through an assault mechanoid and needed to understand how
subject_story->researched the effects of ammunition density on armor

ResearchProjectDef.label: rocketswarm launcher
ResearchProjectDef.description: Produce rocketswarm launchers, single-burst turrets which can devastate a wide area at a key moment in battle.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->testified about the use of rocketswarm launchers against civilian targets
subject_story->constructed last-ditch defenses, including traps and launchers, in case the settlement was ever threatened
subject_story->started by constructing primitive rockets to reach space, but the high failure rate led to them being repurposed as weapons

ResearchProjectDef.label: starflight basics
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct the structural and supportive elements of a starship. This is the first step in building a ship to leave this star system.
ResearchProjectDef.discoveredLetterText:
Escaping from this planet - it would be freedom at last, and maybe a return home.

But also incredibly dangerous.

A new Ship category is available in the Architect menu from which you may build ship parts once the appropriate technology is researched. Ships require several different parts in order to launch, including a ship reactor.

Ship reactors take 15 days to charge up and many desperate souls want off this planet. Once you begin that process, the ship reactor will emit an energy signature detectable from thousands of kilometers away. Raiders will flock to attack you in waves, with an intensity you've never seen. Mechanoids are also known to be attracted to such energy signatures.

It won't start until you activate your ship's reactor, but when it does, it'll be ferocious. You'll need to stockpile resources, weapons, and defenses for the onslaught if you hope to escape alive.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->recruited starship engineers for a glitterworld fleet
subject_story->was a structural designer in an urbworld skyripper district
subject_story->harvested shipwrecks in the debris belt of a deadworld

ResearchProjectDef.label: vacuum cryptosleep casket
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct hardened cryptosleep caskets tough enough to be exposed to vacuum, for transporting people on the years-long journey between stars.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->replaced the failed cryptosleep caskets on the CMC Celeste, so the old generation ship could be used again
subject_story->was accidentally ejected in deep space, surviving in a self-designed casket for two months
subject_story->lectured on the differences between planetary- and starship-grade equipment

ResearchProjectDef.label: starship reactor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a long-duration nuclear reactor to power a starship. Note that reactors have a long startup process that will attract raiders.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->constructed a new reactor for a colony ship, but never lived to see it lift off
subject_story->defended the ship whilst the reactor span up, against raiders desperate to get off-world
subject_story->used a starship reactor as the back-up power for a genebank buried beneath the planet's ice-cap

ResearchProjectDef.label: Johnson-Tanaka drive
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct a Johnson-Tanaka drive for a ship. The JT drive can push you to other stars by leveraging quantum scale effects to beam momentum to distant stars. Of course, as with all starships, it still takes many years to get anywhere.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->lectured in the university on Johnson, Tanaka and quantum-scale effects
subject_story->constructed a Johnson-Tanaka drive from first principles for a thesis
subject_story->maintained a Johnson-Tanaka drive for two decades, as the ship traveled between the stars

ResearchProjectDef.label: machine persuasion
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a reward-signal system to persuade an existing persona core into serving as a ship's machine captain. Since people sleep during interstellar travel, a persona core is necessary to handle the complex decisions of a years-long starflight.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->regained control of an aberrant ship's core with careful reconditioning
subject_story->set up colony-management simulations to occupy the ship's core during the many years of interstellar travel
subject_story->kept a ship's core company during a 'short' interstellar trip, learning much about cores in the process

ResearchProjectDef.label: starflight sensors
ResearchProjectDef.description: Construct long-range sensors for a starship. These sensors are essential for navigation, communication, and threat avoidance.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->used prototype starship sensors to detect an incoming extinction-level asteroid and evacuate the planet
subject_story->was employed as navigator and cook on a Glitterworld star-yacht
subject_story->refined the design of long-range sensors, improving their utility

ResearchTabDef.label: Main
ResearchTabDef.generalDescription: Unlock new technologies by researching at a research bench. You can only have one active project at a time.

RitualOutcomeEffectDef.description: Depending on ritual quality, participants will get between {MINMOOD} and {MAXMOOD} mood for {MOODDAYS} days.
