{PAWN_pronoun} gets a mood bonus if awake at night (23h-6h) and mood loss if awake during the day (11h-18h).

{PAWN_pronoun} doesn't get a mood penalty for being in the dark.

li.label: greedy
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} needs a really impressive bedroom. {PAWN_pronoun} gets a mood loss if {PAWN_pronoun} doesn't get what {PAWN_pronoun} wants.

li.label: jealous
li.description: For {PAWN_nameDef}, it's degrading to have a less impressive bedroom than someone else. {PAWN_pronoun} gets a mood loss if any colonist has a more impressive bedroom.

li.label: ascetic
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has forsaken physical comforts and enjoyments in favor of a simple, pure lifestyle. {PAWN_pronoun} will become unhappy if {PAWN_pronoun} has a bedroom that's too impressive. {PAWN_pronoun} also dislikes fancy food and prefers to eat raw. {PAWN_pronoun} never judges others by their appearance.

li.label: gay
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is romantically attracted to people of {PAWN_possessive} own gender.

li.label: bisexual
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is romantically attracted to both men and women.

li.label: asexual
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has no sexual attraction to anyone at all.

li.label: annoying voice
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef}'s voice has a particularly grating, nasal quality to it, and {PAWN_pronoun} tends to talk in barked, garbled phrases. This predisposes others to dislike {PAWN_objective}.

li.label: creepy breathing
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} breathes heavily all the time, and sweats constantly. People find it creepy.

li.label: pyromaniac
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} loves fire. {PAWN_pronoun} will never extinguish fires, and will occasionally go on random fire starting sprees. {PAWN_pronoun} will be happy around flames, and happier when wielding an incendiary weapon.

li.label: wimp
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is weak and cowardly. Even a little pain will immobilize {PAWN_objective}.

li.label: nimble
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has remarkable kinesthetic intelligence. {PAWN_pronoun} seems to dance around danger with preternatural grace.

li.label: fast learner
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has a knack for learning. {PAWN_pronoun} picks things up much faster than others.

li.label: slow learner
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is slow on the uptake. {PAWN_pronoun} learns much slower than others.

li.label: undergrounder
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has no need to experience the outdoors or light. {PAWN_pronoun} will never feel cooped up or get cabin fever and is not bothered by darkness. However, {PAWN_nameDef} will be unhappy while outdoors.

li.label: body modder
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} feels limited in {PAWN_possessive} feeble human body. {PAWN_pronoun} often dreams of being enhanced with artificial body parts or xenogenetics.

li.label: body purist
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} believes the human body is limited for a reason. To {PAWN_objective}, artificial body parts and xenogenes are unethical and disgusting.

li.label: misandrist
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} really dislikes and distrusts men.

li.label: misogynist
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} really dislikes and distrusts women.

li.label: great memory
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has a fantastic memory for detail. {PAWN_pronoun} will lose unused skills at half the rate of other people.

li.label: tough
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has thick skin, dense flesh, and durable bones. {PAWN_pronoun} takes much less damage than other people from the same blows. {PAWN_pronoun} is extremely hard to kill.

li.label: tortured artist
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} feels alienated and misunderstood by other human beings. {PAWN_pronoun} will have a constant mood debuff, but gain a chance (50%) to get a creativity inspiration after a mental break.
li.mentalBreakInspirationGainReasonText: As a suffering tortured artist, [PAWN_nameIndef] has experienced an inspiration.

li.label: gourmand
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef}'s life revolves around food. {PAWN_pronoun} gets hungry quickly, and will occasionally be overcome with the urge to eat ravenously, even when not hungry.

li.label: quick sleeper
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} doesn't need as much sleep as the average person. Whether {PAWN_pronoun}'s sleeping on a bed or on the ground, {PAWN_pronoun} will be fully rested in about two thirds the usual time.

li.label: slowpoke
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is always falling behind the group whenever [PAWN_pronoun] goes anywhere.

li.label: fast walker
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] likes to be where [PAWN_pronoun]'s going. [PAWN_pronoun] walks quicker than most people.

li.label: jogger
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] always moves with a sense of urgency - so much so that others often fail to keep up.

li.label: chemical fascination
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is utterly fascinated with chemical sources of enjoyment. Consuming recreational drugs will create a good mood, while abstaining will lead to increasing frustration over time and possibly drug binges. [PAWN_pronoun] will ignore directives to not use recreational drugs, and will consume more than a normal person.

li.label: chemical interest
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has an unusual interest in chemical sources of enjoyment. Consuming recreational drugs will create a good mood, while abstaining will lead to increasing frustration over time and possible drug binges. [PAWN_pronoun] will ignore directives to not use recreational drugs, and will consume more than a normal person.

li.label: teetotaler
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] abhors the idea of gaining pleasure from chemicals. [PAWN_pronoun] strictly avoids alcohol and recreational drugs.

li.label: sanguine
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is just naturally upbeat about [PAWN_possessive] situation, pretty much all the time, no matter what it is.

li.label: optimist
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is naturally optimistic about life. It's hard to get [PAWN_objective] down.

li.label: pessimist
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] tends to look on the bad side of life.

li.label: depressive
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is perenially unhappy. [PAWN_pronoun] has trouble sustaining a good mood even when everything is fine.

li.label: iron-willed
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef]'s will is an iron shield. [PAWN_pronoun] keeps going through thick and thin, when others broke down long before.

li.label: steadfast
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is mentally tough and won't break down under stresses that would crack most people.

li.label: nervous
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] tends to crack under pressure.

li.label: volatile
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is on a hair-trigger all the time. [PAWN_pronoun] is the first to break in any tough situation.

li.label: neurotic
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] likes to have things squared away. [PAWN_pronoun] will work harder than most to attain this state of affairs, but [PAWN_possessive] nerves can get the better of [PAWN_objective].

li.label: very neurotic
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] feels constantly nervous about everything that has to get done. [PAWN_pronoun] will work extremely hard to attain this state of affairs, but [PAWN_possessive] nerves can easily get the better of [PAWN_objective].

li.label: industrious
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has an easy time staying on-task and focused, and gets things done much faster than the average person.

li.label: hard worker
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is a natural hard worker and will finish tasks faster than most.

li.label: lazy
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is a little bit lazy.

li.label: slothful
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] loves idleness and hates anything productive. [PAWN_pronoun] moves slowly and rarely stays focused on a task.

li.label: psychically hypersensitive
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef]'s mind is like a psychic tuning fork. [PAWN_pronoun] is extremely sensitive to psychic phenomena.

li.label: psychically sensitive
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef]'s mind is unusually sensitive to psychic phenomena.

li.label: psychically dull
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef]'s mind is psychically out of tune with others. [PAWN_pronoun] isn't as affected by psychic phenomena.

li.label: psychically deaf
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef]'s mind works on a psychic frequency different from everyone else. [PAWN_pronoun] just isn't affected by psychic phenomena.

li.label: careful shooter
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] takes more time to aim when shooting. [PAWN_pronoun] shoots less often than others, but with more accuracy.

li.label: trigger-happy
li.description: Pew! Pew! Pew! [PAWN_nameDef] just likes pulling the trigger. [PAWN_pronoun] shoots faster than others, but less accurately.

li.label: beautiful
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is exceptionally beautiful, with an exotic-yet-familiar facial structure and an arresting gaze. People are attracted to [PAWN_objective] before [PAWN_pronoun] even opens [PAWN_possessive] mouth.

li.label: pretty
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has a pretty face, which predisposes people to like [PAWN_objective].

li.label: ugly
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is somewhat ugly. This subtly repels others during social interactions.

li.label: staggeringly ugly
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is staggeringly ugly. [PAWN_possessive] face looks like a cross between a drawing by an untalented child, a malformed fetus in a jar of formaldehyde, and a piece of modern art. Others must exert conscious effort to look at [PAWN_objective] while conversing.

li.label: super-immune
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has a naturally powerful immune system. [PAWN_pronoun] will gain immunity much faster than a normal person would, and can survive illnesses that would kill others.

li.label: sickly
li.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has an awful immune system. [PAWN_pronoun] gets sick more often than usual, frequently with illnesses that nobody in the colony has been afflicted by.

ConceptDef.label: World view camera movement
ConceptDef.helpText: Zoom with the MOUSE WHEEL or {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out} keys.\n\nPan with the {Key:MapDolly_Up}-{Key:MapDolly_Left}-{Key:MapDolly_Down}-{Key:MapDolly_Right} keys, or by MIDDLE-CLICKING and DRAGGING.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: Zoom with {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out}.\n\nPan with the D-pad or by using the touch screen.

ConceptDef.label: Reforming caravans
ConceptDef.helpText: After an encounter, you can easily re-form a caravan by using the RE-FORM CARAVAN command in the World view.

ConceptDef.label: Rescuing
ConceptDef.helpText: To rescue a wounded person, select a healthy colonist and then right-click on the wounded one.\n\nIf you rescue a non-colonist, they won't necessarily join your colony. They may simply walk away after healing. If you want to guarantee that they join, capture them and recruit them.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: To rescue a wounded person, select a healthy colonist and then press the left trigger button on the wounded one.\n\nIf you rescue a non-colonist, they won't necessarily join your colony. They may simply walk away after healing. If you want to guarantee that they join, capture them and recruit them.

ConceptDef.label: Capturing
ConceptDef.helpText:
When an enemy is downed on the ground but not dead, you can CAPTURE them.

To capture, select a colonist, right-click on the incapacitated enemy, and select Capture.

You'll need an extra bed marked for prisoner use.
ConceptDef.helpTextController:
When an enemy is downed on the ground but not dead, you can CAPTURE them.

To capture, select a colonist, press the left trigger button on the incapacitated enemy, and select Capture.

You'll need an extra bed marked for prisoner use.

ConceptDef.label: Shield belts
ConceptDef.helpText: Shield belts stop ranged attacks from coming in or out. They have no effect on melee attacks.\n\nTo fight against shield belts, either concentrate a lot of gunfire on the target, or fight hand-to-hand.

ConceptDef.label: Interacting with traders
ConceptDef.helpText: You can talk to people with ? over their heads.\n\nSelect a colonist and right-click on the character with ? attached to their head.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: You can talk to people with ? over their heads.\n\nSelect a colonist and press the left trigger button on the character with ? attached to their head.

ConceptDef.label: Drafting for combat
ConceptDef.helpText:
To control colonists directly for combat, Draft them by selecting them and hitting the DRAFT button.

A drafted colonist will do only what you tell them, and can only take combat actions. Those with weapons will use them when possible.

Don't leave colonists Drafted forever - they'll starve and become unhappy.

ConceptDef.label: Positioning fighters
ConceptDef.helpText: Right-click and drag to have your drafted fighters form a line.\n\nSpread out - bunched-up targets are easy to hit!
ConceptDef.helpTextController: Hold the left trigger button and drag to have your drafted fighters form a line.\n\nSpread out - bunched-up targets are easy to hit!

ConceptDef.label: Build orbital trade beacon
ConceptDef.helpText: To send items or silver to orbital traders, you must build an ORBITAL TRADE BEACON and place a stockpile of items near it.

ConceptDef.label: Animals will attack doors
ConceptDef.helpText: Manhunting animals will attack doors if they see one of your colonists moving through them. They will also attack inactive turrets.

ConceptDef.label: Bills tab
ConceptDef.helpText: To make colonists work at a table, select the table and open the Bills tab. Here, you can say what meals to cook, what things to craft, what creatures to butcher.

ConceptDef.label: Using the comms console
ConceptDef.helpText: To communicate, select a colonist and right-click on the comms console.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: To communicate, select a colonist and press the left trigger button on the comms console.

ConceptDef.label: Drug addiction
ConceptDef.helpText:
You can inspect your colonists' desire to take a drug in their Needs tab.

As long as their need level is at zero, their addiction changes to a "withdrawal" state which can have various negative side effects.

However, after long enough in withdrawal, their addiction will end and the drug need will disappear.

ConceptDef.label: Drug policies
ConceptDef.helpText:
You can assign colonists to take specific drugs on a specific schedule. For example, you can make them take infection-blocking drugs regularly, or drink a beer a day to stay happy.

Open the ASSIGN tab and press the 'Manage drug policies' button. Create a new drug policy. Then, you can assign this policy to colonists.

Colonists can still take drugs not in their policy. You can tell them what to do, but they also follow their own desires!

ConceptDef.label: TV for sick people
ConceptDef.helpText: Sick people can watch TV while laying in bed.

ConceptDef.label: Prisoner tab
ConceptDef.helpText:
Look in a prisoner's 'Prisoner' tab to set how they'll be treated.

You can set whether they'll be recruited, ignored, or executed, and what kind of medical care they get. You can set food restrictions for the prisoner in their health tab.

Colonists with the Warden work type will interact with the prisoner.

ConceptDef.label: Set what plant to grow
ConceptDef.helpText: You can set what to plant in a growing zone. You can even grow trees!\n\nJust select the growing zone, open the Growing tab, and click the 'plant' button.

ConceptDef.label: Drug burning
ConceptDef.helpText: Drugs can be useful, but can also lead to harmful addictions.\n\nIf you want to avoid drugs in your colony, you have the option of burning them at a campfire.

ConceptDef.label: Door opening speeds
ConceptDef.helpText: Doors open at different speeds depending on what they're made of.\n\nWarning: Stone doors open very slowly. Anyone passing through will be significantly slowed down.

ConceptDef.label: Order queueing
ConceptDef.helpText: When giving commands to pawns, you can queue up multiple orders by holding "shift". This also works when giving jobs to undrafted pawns.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: When giving commands to pawns, you can queue up multiple orders by holding {Key:QueueOrder}. This also works when giving jobs to undrafted pawns.

ConceptDef.label: Shelves
ConceptDef.helpText: Shelves store three times as much as empty ground. Items on shelves will also never deteriorate and don't affect the beauty of their surroundings.\n\nYou can link shelves into groups and configure them as one. First, select two or more shelves, then click 'Link storage settings'.

ConceptDef.label: books
ConceptDef.helpText:
Colonists read books for recreation, to gain skills, to unlock research, and more. You can see a specific book's effects by selecting it and opening its 'Details' tab.

To choose what colonists will read, open the ASSIGN tab and configure READING POLICIES.

Store books in bookcases to passively enhance intellectual and reading work done nearby, and increase the beauty of the bookcase. Bookcases passively increase research speed, XP gained from reading, and recreation gained from reading in the same room.

ConceptDef.label: Camera dolly
ConceptDef.helpText: Move the camera by clicking and dragging the MOUSE BUTTON 3 (middle button) or with the {Key:MapDolly_Up}-{Key:MapDolly_Left}-{Key:MapDolly_Down}-{Key:MapDolly_Right} keys.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: Move the camera by using the D-pad.

ConceptDef.label: Camera zoom
ConceptDef.helpText: Zoom in and out with the MOUSEWHEEL or the {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out} keys.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: Zoom in and out with {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out}.

ConceptDef.label: Time controls
ConceptDef.helpText: You can speed up time.\n\nTry controlling time with the {Key:TimeSpeed_Normal}, {Key:TimeSpeed_Fast}, and {Key:TimeSpeed_Superfast} keys, or with the time controls in the bottom right.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: You can speed up time.\n\nTry controlling time with {Key:TimeSpeed_Faster} and {Key:TimeSpeed_Slower}, or with the time controls in the bottom right.

ConceptDef.label: Pausing
ConceptDef.helpText:
Hit {Key:TogglePause} to pause or unpause the game.

You can give orders while paused.

Remember this - if things get hectic, just hit {Key:TogglePause}!

ConceptDef.label: Stockpiles
ConceptDef.helpText: Your colonists need somewhere to store items. Designate a STOCKPILE for them to store things.\n\nFind the stockpile in the ZONES section of the ARCHITECT menu in the lower-left.

ConceptDef.label: Forbid and allow
ConceptDef.helpText: Colonists will not interact with items marked FORBIDDEN.\n\nForbidden items have a small red X attached. Select a forbidden item and use the controls at the bottom to ALLOW it.

ConceptDef.label: Growing zones
ConceptDef.helpText: To grow food, place GROWING ZONES using the Architect menu.\n\nThey can only be placed on fertile ground.

ConceptDef.label: Equipping weapons
ConceptDef.helpText: Your colonists arrived with some weapons. Equip them!\n\nSelect each colonist and right-click on the weapon you want them to equip.
ConceptDef.helpTextController: Your colonists arrived with some weapons. Equip them!\n\nSelect each colonist and press the left trigger on the weapon you want them to equip.

ConceptDef.label: Alerts
ConceptDef.helpText: The alerts at the right edge of the screen tell you about issues that need your attention.\n\nKeep an eye on the alerts.

ConceptDef.label: Mining
ConceptDef.helpText: You can designate where to mine by opening the ARCHITECT menu and selecting the ORDERS tab.\n\nSome mineable blocks yield STEEL, GOLD, PLASTEEL, and other useful materials.

ConceptDef.label: Work settings
ConceptDef.helpText:
You can set each colonist's work settings in the WORK tab at the bottom left of the screen.

They will always do the highest priority work that they can find.

If nobody has a certain work type assigned, or if they are busy with higher-priority tasks, it will never get done.

ConceptDef.label: Forbidding doors
ConceptDef.helpText: You can FORBID doors so colonists and tame animals won't go through them.\n\nNote that this isn't a door lock. Doors are always locked, so enemies can't pass freely. Forbidding just directs your colonists not to use the door. Colonists who are going crazy might use the door anyway.

ConceptDef.label: Cover and shooting
ConceptDef.helpText:
The most important thing to do in ranged combat is to use cover.

Cover only works if your colonist is touching it, and it is between your colonist and the enemy.

You can also place colonists behind wall corners. They will lean out to shoot.

Most things can be used as cover, but some things are better than others. Hiding behind a tree is better than nothing, but hiding behind sandbags is better than using a tree.

ConceptDef.label: Forming caravans
ConceptDef.helpText: You can form a caravan to send groups of people traveling across the planet!\n\nIn the WORLD tab, select your home base and click the "form caravan" button.

ConceptDef.label: Animal taming
ConceptDef.helpText:
You can assign colonists to tame a wild animal with the TAME designator.

Colonists will offer the animal food and attempt to tame it.

Beware: Some animals can respond violently to failed taming attempts.

ConceptDef.label: Animal training
ConceptDef.helpText: You can assign a tame animal to be trained in specific skills on its TRAINING tab or on the ANIMALS tab.\n\nAnimals can't be trained continuously; they need time between training sessions.

ConceptDef.label: Info card
ConceptDef.helpText: The info card shows you detailed statistics about any item, person, or construction.\n\nSelect a person or item and open their info card with the 'i' button on the inspect pane.

ConceptDef.label: Storage tab
ConceptDef.helpText:
You can configure stockpiles and storage buildings by selecting them and opening the STORAGE TAB above the bottom-left inspector pane.

In the storage tab of a stockpile, you can expand categories to allow or deny specific items. Click the triangles to the left of category names.

You can change the PRIORITY of storage. Colonists will fill higher-priority storage first, and move items from lower to higher priority.

ConceptDef.label: Home area
ConceptDef.helpText: The HOME AREA tells your colonists which area to clean and where to extinguish fires.\n\nDefine the HOME AREA with the Zones category under the Architect menu.

ConceptDef.label: Spoilage and freezers
ConceptDef.helpText:
Most foodstuffs will spoil after a relatively short time.

To prevent this, you can build a walk-in freezer.

To build a freezer, construct a closed room, and put one or two coolers into the wall. Set the coolers to a negative target temperature.

Frozen foods won't ever spoil.

ConceptDef.label: Item deterioration
ConceptDef.helpText: Items left outdoors will slowly deteriorate.\n\nIf you want to store items long-term, keep them in a roofed room.

ConceptDef.label: Hostility response modes
ConceptDef.helpText: You can configure how colonists should automatically respond to threats like predatory animals.\n\nChoose from FLEE, ATTACK, and IGNORE modes in the ASSIGN menu.

ConceptDef.label: Allowed areas
ConceptDef.helpText:
Colonists and colony animals can be assigned to ALLOWED AREAS. This forbids them from taking destinations outside their allowed area.

This can be used to, for example, forbid colonists from going outside.

You can create multiple allowed areas and assign them to different colonists and animals.

Create, delete, and assign allowed areas in the SCHEDULE tab.

Paint allowed areas onto the map using the EXPAND ALLOWED AREA and CLEAR ALLOWED AREA designators in the Architect tab.

ConceptDef.label: Medical operations
ConceptDef.helpText: To assign a medical operation, like organ harvesting or prosthetics installation, open a colonist's HEALTH tab, then switch to the OPERATIONS sub-tab.

ConceptDef.label: Time assignments
ConceptDef.helpText: You can modify what time of day colonists should do different activities using the SCHEDULE tab.

ConceptDef.label: Manual work priorities
ConceptDef.helpText:
One of the most important parts of RimWorld is choosing good work settings for your colonists.

Poor work settings can leave essential work unfinished for a long time while colonists waste time on unimportant tasks.

To give more control over what work colonists do, you can use the Manual Priorities mode in the WORK tab.

In this mode, each colonist has a priority number for each work type. Colonists will do priority 1 work from left to right, then priority 2 work from left to right, and so on.

Intelligent use of these setting is essential for a large, well-automated colony.

ConceptDef.label: Getting more traders
ConceptDef.helpText:
More trader caravans will come to visit you if you're allied with more factions.

If you have no allies, no caravans will ever visit!

You can also pay allies to send trade caravans by calling them on the comms console.

ConceptDef.label: Tile inspector
ConceptDef.helpText: You can inspect the details of a tile by holding {Key:ShowCellInspector}. This displays the contents of a tile, room information, beauty information, and more.

ConceptDef.label: Outfits
ConceptDef.helpText:
Colonists will automatically try to wear the newest, highest-quality apparel they can.

You don't need to manually assign each piece of apparel to colonists (though you can, if you wish).

To assign colonists restrictions on how to dress, open the ASSIGN tab, use the "Manage apparel policies" dialog box to design a new outfit, and then assign the outfit to colonists.

ConceptDef.label: Fire preparation
ConceptDef.helpText:
Fires can easily burn down a colony. To defeat them, you must prepare before they happen. 
These design elements can help reduce the damage from fires: 
1. Instead of constructing one super-building, build separate buildings with spaces in between. 
2. Use less flammable materials. Wood is cheap and fast - but very flammable. 
3. Build firebreaks to stop wildfires approaching your base. A strip of concrete floor 3 or 4 cells wide will generally stop an advancing fire.

ConceptDef.label: History tab
ConceptDef.helpText: You can see a record of your colony's fortunes over time in the HISTORY tab at the bottom of the screen.

ConceptDef.label: Clicking messages
ConceptDef.helpText: You can click on the notifications in the top-left of the screen to instantly center the camera on their subject.

ConceptDef.label: Shot accuracy tooltip
ConceptDef.helpText: You can see the exact calculations behind the accuracy of any shot.\n\nTo do so, select the shooter, then rest the mouse over the target. The tooltip will show the chance to hit, and a breakdown of the contribution of various to-hit chance multipliers.

ConceptDef.label: Friendly fire safety
ConceptDef.helpText:
Friendly fire never occurs if the shooter is close to their ally.

For example, you can safely put a sword-wielding colonist directly in front of a gun-wielding one. The shooter will fire over their friend's shoulder.

This is a good way to combine ranged and melee fighters.

ConceptDef.label: Trade goods and trade beacons
ConceptDef.helpText: To send items or silver to orbital traders, you must build an ORBITAL TRADE BEACON and place a stockpile of items near it.

ConceptDef.label: Arresting worsens faction relations
ConceptDef.helpText:
Warning: The person you are trying to arrest may not go quietly.

If you arrest a non-colonist or a colonist from another faction, their entire faction may become your enemy. 

This arrest has a {0} chance of succeeding, based on the social skill of the arrester.

ConceptDef.label: Flick designations only designate
ConceptDef.helpText: Note: This only designates that a colonist should flick the switch.\n\nNothing will actually happen until a colonist comes and flicks the switch by hand.

ConceptDef.label: Maximum number of player colonies
ConceptDef.helpText:
Warning: RimWorld is designed to be played with one player colony at a time. Multiple player colonies are allowed as an experimental testing feature only.

Playing with multiple colonies will cause gameplay imbalances and split your focus, as well as likely causing performance slowdowns.

We recommend that you play with the one-colony maximum the game was designed for, at least for your first few games.

ConceptDef.label: Trading permit requirements
ConceptDef.helpText: Trading here requires the title of {0}.\n\nEnsure any trade caravan you send has someone with the title of {0} or higher.

ConceptDef.label: Steam Deck controls
ConceptDef.helpText: Use the trackpad to move the cursor and the right trigger button to click. Press {Key:Accept} to accept and {Key:Cancel} to go back.

ConceptDef.label: Steam Deck controls
ConceptDef.helpText: Press X to open the architect menu and {Key:TogglePause} to pause and resume the game. Use triggers for primary and secondary clicks. Zoom in and out and scroll through lists with {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out}. Press and hold the L5 back button to pan the camera with the touch screen and simulate secondary clicks.

InstructionDef.text:
Welcome to RimWorld!

This page configures how your world should be generated.

The default settings here are good - go ahead and click GENERATE!
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Click GENERATE to generate your world.

InstructionDef.text:
Here you choose your starting site.

Click a temperate forest (light green) with no brown hills. Then click NEXT.

Optionally, you can use the TERRAIN tab to view information about the selected tile.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please choose a temperate forest site with no hills (light green with no brown dots).

InstructionDef.text:
Now you choose which characters you want to use.

DRAG a character from the "left behind" part of the character list (at the bottom) into the "selected" part (at the top).

Optionally, clicking a character will allow you inspect him or her.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please drag a character from the "left behind" group (at the bottom-left) into the "selected" group (at the upper-left).

InstructionDef.text: If you don't like a character, you can regenerate them!\n\nClick the RANDOMIZE button to randomize the character.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please click the RANDOMIZE button to randomize the character.

InstructionDef.text:
Great!

Reorder and randomize more if you want - but don't try to get the perfect characters. Everyone has flaws, and it makes the story more interesting!

You can also re-name the characters by clicking on their names.

Click START when you're ready.

Here you are on the surface!

Now try moving the camera around.

Use the {Key:MapDolly_Up}-{Key:MapDolly_Left}-{Key:MapDolly_Down}-{Key:MapDolly_Right} keys, or click and drag with the middle mouse button.

Try it now!
InstructionDef.textController:
Here you are on the surface!

Now try moving the camera around with the left joystick.

Try it now!

InstructionDef.text:
Great!

You can also zoom in and out with the mouse wheel, or the {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out} keys.

Try it now!
InstructionDef.textController:
Great!

You can also zoom in and out with {Key:MapZoom_In} and {Key:MapZoom_Out}.

Try it now!

InstructionDef.text:
You can pause time.

This means you never need to rush. You can always pause and take your time to issue orders.

Try pausing with the {Key:TogglePause} key, or by using the time controls in the bottom right.
InstructionDef.textController:
You can pause time.

This means you never need to rush. You can always pause and take your time to issue orders.

Try pausing with the {Key:TogglePause} button, or by using the time controls in the bottom right.

InstructionDef.text: You can also speed up time.\n\nTry controlling time with the {Key:TimeSpeed_Normal}, {Key:TimeSpeed_Fast}, and {Key:TimeSpeed_Superfast} keys, or with the time controls in the bottom right.
InstructionDef.textController: You can also speed up time.\n\nTry controlling time with {Key:TimeSpeed_Faster} and {Key:TimeSpeed_Slower}, or with the time controls in the bottom right.

InstructionDef.text:
Great!

Now, make a stockpile so your colonists know where to keep items.

1. Click ARCHITECT tab in the bottom left.
2. Click the ZONE/AREA category.
3. Select the CREATE STOCKPILE tool.
4. Click and drag out a square as indicated on the map.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please make a stockpile on the indicated area.

InstructionDef.text: Right-click to get out of stockpile designating mode.
InstructionDef.textController: Press left trigger button to get out of stockpile designating mode.

InstructionDef.text:
To allow your colonists to bring your items to the stockpile, you must remove the items' "forbidden" designation.

1. Clicking your starting items to select them.
2. Click the ALLOW toggle button to allow them.

(Pro tip: Double-click an item to select all on screen of the same type.)

Alternatively, you can:
1. Click ARCHITECT.
2. Click ORDERS.
3. Click ALLOW.
4. Drag out a shape covering all forbidden items to allow them.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please allow your starting items.

InstructionDef.text:
Awesome! Next, we'll build a room.

1. Click ARCHITECT.
2. Click STRUCTURE.
3. Select WALL.
4. Select WOOD as the material.
5. Drag out four walls to form the shape indicated on the map.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build wooden walls along the edges of the highlighted rectangle.

InstructionDef.text: Now just place a DOOR over any one of the room walls.\n\nDOOR is right beside WALL in the ARCHITECT menu.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build a door over one wall
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build a wooden door over one of your room walls.

InstructionDef.text:
Your colonists will now build the room!

Now they need somewhere to sleep. Place three BEDS inside the room.

Find them in the FURNITURE category.

You can use the {Key:Designator_RotateLeft} and {Key:Designator_RotateRight} keys to rotate the building.
InstructionDef.textController:
Your colonists will now build the room!

Now they need somewhere to sleep. Place three BEDS inside the room.

Find them in the FURNITURE category.

You can rotate the building by pressing the rotate buttons on the left.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build three beds inside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build wooden beds inside the room.

InstructionDef.text: You'll also want some light inside, or your colonists will get grumpy in the dark.\n\nBuild a TORCH LAMP inside the room.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build a torch lamp inside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build a torch lamp inside the room.

InstructionDef.text: So your pet will sleep inside with you, place an ANIMAL SLEEPING SPOT inside the room.\n\nSleeping spots aren't real buildings - they're just spots on the ground designated for a sleeping.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build an animal sleeping spot\ninside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please place an animal sleeping spot inside the room.

InstructionDef.text: Your colonists need sources of recreation or they'll get sad over time.\n\nBuild a HORSESHOES pin outside, near the room.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build a horseshoes pin\noutside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please place a horseshoes pin somewhere near the room.

InstructionDef.text:
The house is being built!

Your colonists will need something to eat, so place a GROWING ZONE as indicated on the map.

This is where your colonists will sow crops.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please make a growing zone on the indicated area.

InstructionDef.text:
You can decide what plant your colonists should sow in a growing zone.

1. Right-click to exit architect mode.
2. Click your growing zone to select it.
3. Click the plant selector at the bottom and change it to rice.
InstructionDef.textController:
You can decide what plant your colonists should sow in a growing zone.

1. Press left trigger button to exit architect mode.
2. Click your growing zone to select it.
3. Click the plant selector at the bottom and change it to rice.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please set your growing zone to grow rice.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Set this growing zone to grow rice

InstructionDef.text:
Have your colonists equip the starting weapons. To equip a weapon:

1. Click a colonist to select them.
2. Right-click the weapon you want to equip.
3. Click 'equip weapon' on the context menu.

Do this for each colonist.
InstructionDef.textController:
Have your colonists equip the starting weapons. To equip a weapon:

1. Click a colonist to select them.
2. Hover over the weapon you want to equip and press left trigger button.
3. Click 'equip weapon' on the context menu.

Do this for each colonist.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please have your colonists equip weapons.

InstructionDef.text:
Excellent!

Now you'll need to make a stove to cook food.

Build a FUELED STOVE inside the room.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build a fueled stove inside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build the fueled stove inside the room you built earlier.

InstructionDef.text:
Colonists need to be told what to cook.

Cooking orders are added on the stove itself. Once a bill has been created, colonists will do the work automatically.

1. Wait for the stove to be built.
2. Click the stove to select it.
3. Open the BILLS tab.
4. Click ADD BILL.
5. Select COOK SIMPLE MEAL on the context menu.
6. Click the + button to increase the count to 10.

Remember, you can speed up time if building is taking too long.

You can also select a colonist and right-click the stove to prioritize building it.
InstructionDef.textController:
Colonists need to be told what to cook.

Cooking orders are added on the stove itself. Once a bill has been created, colonists will do the work automatically.

1. Wait for the stove to be built.
2. Click the stove to select it.
3. Open the BILLS tab.
4. Click ADD BILL.
5. Select COOK SIMPLE MEAL on the context menu.
6. Click the + button to increase the count to 10.

Remember, you can speed up time if building is taking too long.

You can also select a colonist and press left trigger button on the stove to prioritize building it.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please add a bill to cook simple meals at your cook stove.

InstructionDef.text:
Now your colonists will cook some food! Tasty!

Next, you'll want to mine some minerals. I've spawned some mineable steel near your base.

Select the MINE designator and drag over the steel to designate it for mining.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please use the 'mine' designator on the compacted steel.

InstructionDef.text:
You'll want to harvest some wood. Designate some trees to be chopped.

Select the CHOP WOOD designator and designate 10 trees to be chopped down.

(Pro tip: You can drag a box over trees to designate several at once.)
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please drag the 'chop wood' designator over some trees.

InstructionDef.text: You can control which colonist does what kind of work.\n\nOpen the WORK tab at the bottom of the screen.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please open the 'Work' tab.

InstructionDef.text:
You can control who does what kinds of work using the checkboxes. Colonists will do tasks in order, from left to right.

Try changing some settings now.

Beware - Colonists always follow their work priorities, even if this makes them do dumb things! Setting up a smart work regime is an important skill in RimWorld. So set the work settings carefully, and review them often!
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please open the 'Work' tab and change some settings.

InstructionDef.text: To advance, you'll need to research new technologies.\n\nBuild a wooden SIMPLE RESEARCH BENCH inside your room.
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Build a wooden simple research bench\ninside the room
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please place a wooden simple research bench inside the room you built earlier.

InstructionDef.text: Excellent! Next, you'll want to select what you want to be researched.\n\nOpen the RESEARCH tab.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please open the 'Research' tab.

InstructionDef.text:
Now just choose whatever you want to be researched first.

You might have to wait for the research bench to be constructed, or for trees to be chopped for wood.

If it's taking too long, use the WORK tab to assign more colonists to Construct.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please choose a research project.

InstructionDef.text:
Next, you'll learn to expand the HOME AREA.

Colonists will clean floors and extinguish fires in the home area only, and ignore fires or filth outside of it.

The home area is added automatically when you build things - but you can also expand it manually.

Select the EXPAND HOME AREA tool and drag out a new area on the map.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please expand the home area a bit, just for practice.

InstructionDef.text:
The BUILD ROOF AREA defines where your colonists will try to build roofs.

It auto-fills when you enclose a new room.

Select the EXPAND BUILD ROOF AREA tool and drag out the shape of a porch roof on the front of the house.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please expand the build roof area a bit, just for practice.

InstructionDef.text: Great! You've now got a basic colony running! Eventually, enemies will raid your colony. It's time to prepare for that.\n\nSelect the SANDBAGS designator and drag the sandbags out at the designated area.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please build sandbags in the highlighted area.

InstructionDef.text:
Let's just wait for all your constructions to be built.

Consider using the WORK tab to assign more colonists to Construct.

Also, you can speed up time to shorten the wait.

Once everything's built, I'll send an attacker to test your defenses!
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please wait for your colonists to finish building the sandbags.

InstructionDef.text:
I've now sent a raider to attack your colony!

1. Pause the game by hitting {Key:TogglePause}!
2. Read the red letter in the bottom-right of the screen.
3. DRAFT your colonists by selecting them and hitting the DRAFT command.
4. Right-click to send them to positions inside the sandbag square, touching the sandbags.
5. Unpause.

Colonists must be touching cover to benefit from it. Once you're in cover, wait for the attacker to approach. Your colonists will shoot automatically.
InstructionDef.textController:
I've now sent a raider to attack your colony!

1. Pause the game by hitting {Key:TogglePause}!
2. Read the red letter in the bottom-right of the screen.
3. DRAFT your colonists by selecting them and hitting the DRAFT command.
4. Press left trigger button to send them to positions inside the sandbag square, touching the sandbags.
5. Unpause.

Colonists must be touching cover to benefit from it. Once you're in cover, wait for the attacker to approach. Your colonists will shoot automatically.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please focus on winning the fight!
InstructionDef.onMapInstruction: Send colonists here\ntouching sandbags for cover

InstructionDef.text: Success! Now UNDRAFT all your colonists using the same command as before.\n\nThis will let them return to their own schedules.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please un-draft your colonists.

InstructionDef.text:
This is the end of the tutorial!

There's still tons more to learn, including prisoners, hunting, trade, animal taming, and much more. But you've got the basics down.

Random incidents were disabled during this tutorial. To begin the real game:

1. Open the MENU tab in the bottom-right.
2. Select OPTIONS.
3. Click the Gameplay button in the left column.
4. Click the Modify button beside Storyteller settings.
5. Select a storyteller and playstyle that appeals to you.

Good luck, and have fun.
InstructionDef.rejectInputMessage: Please choose a storyteller in the Options menu to end the tutorial.

WeatherDef.label: clear
WeatherDef.description: A clear day. No penalties or modifiers.

WeatherDef.label: fog
WeatherDef.description: Fog reduces the accuracy of ranged weapons.

WeatherDef.label: rain
WeatherDef.description: Rain reduces the accuracy of ranged weapons, extinguishes fire, and slows people down.

WeatherDef.label: dry thunderstorm
WeatherDef.description: Dry thunderstorms are dangerous because the lightning can start fires and there is no rain to put them out.

WeatherDef.label: rainy thunderstorm
WeatherDef.description: The lightning will start fires, but the rain will put it out. The rain also reduces movement speed and shooting accuracy.

WeatherDef.label: hard snow
WeatherDef.description: Snow reduces the accuracy of ranged weapons, extinguishes fire, and slows people down.

WeatherDef.label: gentle snow
WeatherDef.description: Snow reduces the accuracy of ranged weapons, extinguishes fire, and slows people down.

WorkGiverDef.label: go to bed for emergency treatment
tend to patients with urgent needs
take patients to bed for operations
take beer out of fermenting barrels

WorkTypeDef.description: Extinguish fires in the colony.
Go to a medical bed for treatment if you have an immediately life-threatening health condition.
Treat the sick, bring them food, cheer them up, and perform assigned surgeries. Doctors will care for both colonists and prisoners.
Rest in bed to recuperate from not-immediately-life-threatening medical problems.
Unskilled and easy tasks. Release prisoners and flick switches on machines.
Manage, feed, chat with, and recruit prisoners.
Tame, train, harvest resources from and slaughter animals.
Prepare meals and butcher meat.
Kill animals which are designated to be hunted.
Build things that you've designated, and fix damaged or broken-down buildings.
Plant seeds, harvest crops, and forage for wild plants.
Digging and drilling.
Cut or harvest plants as designated.
Create weapons and tools from raw materials, either as a blacksmith or by machining.
Create apparel from raw materials.
Create beautiful works of art from raw materials.
Do general low-skilled labor at work stations. This includes stonecutting, smelting, and more.
Carry things to where they need to be.
Clear snow and clean the floor in the home area.
Perform research work.

WorldObjectDef.Name: Settlement
WorldObjectDef.label: settlement
WorldObjectDef.description: A base of one of the factions.

WorldObjectDef.label: landed ship
WorldObjectDef.description: The location of a hidden ship which can help you escape the planet.

WorldObjectDef.label: peace talks
WorldObjectDef.description: A site designated for peace talks.

WorldObjectDef.label: camp
WorldObjectDef.description: A caravan has set up camp here temporarily.

AbilityDef.label: bloodfeed
AbilityDef.description: Bite the target and extract hemogen directly from their blood. The target will lose blood and will be horrified by the interaction, but will be otherwise unharmed. A fast-acting coagulant will seal the wound to prevent bleeding.\n\nCan only target non-hemogenic humans. Hemogen gain is affected by the target's body size.

AbilityDef.label: coagulate
AbilityDef.description: Use special glands in the wrists to quickly tend someone's wounds.

AbilityDef.label: implant genes
AbilityDef.description: Implant this person's xenogenes into a willing subject using a special injector organ. If this person's genes are currently regrowing, they will implant their xenogerm and die in the process.\n\nWhen implanted, a xenogerm will overwrite the target's xenogenes. Germline genes will be unaffected.

AbilityDef.label: piercing spine
AbilityDef.description: Use a hemogenic chemical reaction to launch a bony spine at the target. The spine exits through the skin from an opening between the collarbones. Given the method of launch, it is surprisingly easy to aim.

AbilityDef.label: resurrect
AbilityDef.description: Use archites in the bloodstream to infuse a corpse's body with new life, repairing degenerated cell structures and kickstarting vital functions. The older and worse-preserved the corpse is, the more likely it is that they will come back with memory loss or health conditions. This ability seems to exhaust the archites somehow, so it can only be used very rarely.

AbilityDef.label: acid spray
AbilityDef.description: Spray a sticky acid substance from glands in the neck up through the mouth and all over the target area. The acid will stick to targets and burn them.

AbilityDef.label: foam spray
AbilityDef.description: Spray thick fire-retardant foam from glands in the neck up through the mouth. The foam will cover a small area and extinguish any fire it touches.

AbilityDef.label: fire spew
AbilityDef.description: Spit a stream of sticky, flammable bile from the mouth. The bile can ignite anything or anyone it hits, and also form flaming pools on the ground.\n\nThe bile is generated and stored by an organ in the neck, along with a separate pouch of hypergolic reactant for ignition.

AbilityDef.Name: LongJump
AbilityDef.label: longjump
AbilityDef.description: Jump to a distant location using super-strong hemogen-powered legs.

AbilityDef.label: fire burst
AbilityDef.description: Emit a burst of burning fuel in all directions to form puddles of ignited liquid on the ground.

AbilityDef.label: animal warcall
AbilityDef.description: With a powerful bellow and psychic connection, call an animal to fight your enemies for a few hours.

AbilityDef.Name: LongJumpMech
AbilityDef.label: mech longjump
AbilityDef.description: Jump to a distant location using special ultrafast mechanoid muscles.

AbilityDef.label: jump launcher
AbilityDef.description: Jump to a distant location using a built-in jump launcher.

AbilityDef.label: mech smokepop
AbilityDef.description: Release compressed smoke from concealed vents. Smoke reduces the accuracy of any shot fired through it, and prevents turrets from locking on entirely.

AbilityDef.label: firefoam pop
AbilityDef.description: Release a fire-retardant foam in a circular area.

AbilityDef.label: resurrect mech
AbilityDef.description: Resurrect a recently-killed mechanoid by externally supercharging its self-repair processes. The mechanoid will come back with some but not all of its wounds healed.

BossgroupDef.leaderDescription: The {LEADERKIND_label} is equipped with a concrete-melting hellsphere cannon. It is slow to charge, but when it fires it will annihilate anything in the blast circle.
The {LEADERKIND_label} has a built-in mech gestator and is capable of deploying war urchin combat mechs.
The {LEADERKIND_label} is a psychically-present mechanoid commander who can resurrect recently-killed mechs and jump long distances. It carries a long-range toxic needle gun.

FactionDef.label: fierce neanderthal tribe
FactionDef.description: An unfriendly, territorial tribe of neanderthals. They are open to peaceful trade, but are otherwise unfriendly and territorial. Warriors from their tribe won't hesitate to bash in the skulls of anyone they deem dangerous. Their numbers, and the extreme amounts of damage they absorb before falling make them serious foes despite their lack of technology and analytical ability.\n\nHaving been on this planet for countless generations, they have no memory of how they got here. They might be the descendants of a neanderthal service caste from a dead civilization, or even the leftovers from some ancient science experiment.

FactionDef.label: yttakin pirates
FactionDef.description: A close-knit band of hulking, fur-bodied pirates of the yttakin xenotype. They refuse to deal with outsiders and are quick to call their animal warriors against those who disrespect them - or whose wealth they intend to take.\n\nOriginally engineered to populate the icy planet Yttak, yttakin now pursue their traditional lifestyle on many worlds.

FactionDef.label: savage impid tribe
FactionDef.description: A vicious tribe of yellow-skinned, fire-spewing impids. This particular tribe has no intention of coexisting peacefully with anyone else. Their warriors are experts at using their natural speed and flame attacks to burn the towns and children of other peoples.\n\nHaving been here for thousands of years, the origins of this tribe are lost in myth. They might descend from a group of settlers who lost their technology, or an impid community in some long-ruined civilization.

FactionDef.label: rough pig union
FactionDef.description: A loose union of hardy pigskin townships. They're willing to make friends, even with thinsnouts, but they're also ready to toss a bomb and gnaw human gristle when it suits them. Treat them with respect and they'll offer a trotter to an ally in need. Turn against them and the last thing you hear might be a triumphant battle squeal.

FactionDef.label: waster pirates
FactionDef.description: A loose collection of violent pirate bands made up primarily of wasters - xenohumans engineered to thrive around toxins and pollution. They have little interest in building, or farming, preferring to take their sustenance from others using violence.\n\nTheir technology level depends mostly on who they've managed to steal from recently. Mostly they carry gunpowder weapons, though some prefer to stab victims at close range.

GameConditionDef.label: acidic smog
GameConditionDef.description: Acidic smog is caused by pollution in nearby world tiles. It slows plant growth, deteriorates exposed items, and reduces mood.\n\nThe current world tile has a nearby pollution score of {NEARBYPOLLUTION}, calculated by adding up pollution of nearby world tiles. This means that, on average, acidic smog will occur every {MTB} days.
GameConditionDef.startMessage: Acidic smog has begun due to pollution in this region of the world.

GeneDef.label: fire spew
GeneDef.description: Carriers are able to spew flammable bile generated by a special organ in their neck. The bile sticks to anything in a small area and can ignite people, objects, and the ground.

GeneDef.label: foam spray
GeneDef.description: Carriers grow glands in the neck that generate and store a fire-retardant foam. They can spew this foam over an area to extinguish fires.

GeneDef.label: longjump legs
GeneDef.description: Carriers have special hemogen-powered muscle fibers in their legs which allow them to jump great distances.

GeneDef.label: animal warcall
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene can perform an animal warcall, using a powerful bellow and psychic connection to call an animal to fight for them.

GeneDef.label: bloodfeeder
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have small retractable fangs and an organ on the roof of the mouth which can extract hemogen from fresh warm blood. They can bite an unresisting person, suck the blood, and gain hemogen directly.

GeneDef.label: coagulate
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have special glands on their hands and wrists, as well as a unique salivary compound that they can use to rapidly tend wounds.

GeneDef.label: gene implanter
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene can implant a copy of their xenogerm into another person through a somewhat gross-looking injector organ. Their own genetic material will then regrow very slowly. If they implant while their genes are regrowing, they will die. Germline genes will be unaffected.

GeneDef.label: piercing spine
GeneDef.description: Carriers grow an opening in their upper chest along with a quiver of keratin spines. Using a hemogen-powered chemical reaction, they can fire these spines at high speed at nearby targets with surprising accuracy.

GeneDef.label: acid spray
GeneDef.description: Carriers grow glands in the neck that generate and store a sticky acid substance, along with acid-tolerant tissues in the mouth. They can spew this acid over an area, where it will stick to enemies and burn them.

GeneDef.label: no hair
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow no hair on the head.

GeneDef.label: short-haired
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene can only grow short hair.

GeneDef.label: long-haired
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow hair on the head very quickly.

GeneDef.label: grayless hair
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene keep their natural hair color as they age.

GeneDef.label: only bushy beards
GeneDef.description: Male carriers of this gene experience rapid beard growth and are uncomfortable cutting their beards.

GeneDef.label: beardless
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow no facial hair.

GeneDef.label: unisex beards
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene always have thick facial hair, even women.

GeneDef.label: ink black skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin a pale black color almost as dark as ink.

GeneDef.label: slate gray skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin slate gray.

GeneDef.label: light gray skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this produce a light-gray pigment in their skin.

GeneDef.label: sheer white skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have sheer white skin, unlike natural skin tones, due to a special engineered reflective cell covering.

GeneDef.label: blue skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin a blue color.

GeneDef.label: purple skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that gives their skin a purple color.

GeneDef.label: pale red skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin a moderate red color.

GeneDef.label: deep red skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a deep-red pigment that gives their skin an almost bloody appearance.

GeneDef.label: pale yellow skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin a grayish yellow color.

GeneDef.label: deep yellow skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that gives their skin a deep yellow color.

GeneDef.label: orange skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that gives their skin an orange color.

GeneDef.label: green skin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that gives their skin a green color.

GeneDef.label: furskin
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow thick fur all over their body, which protects them from cold temperatures.

GeneDef.label: red eyes
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have deeply red-pigmented eyes.

GeneDef.label: gray eyes
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have pale white-gray eyes.

GeneDef.label: heavy brow
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a prominent brow.

GeneDef.label: furry tail
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow a fluffy tail which partially protects them from cold temperatures.

GeneDef.label: smooth tail
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow a slender tail that can act as a dexterous fifth limb.

GeneDef.label: facial ridges
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow raised ridges of skin on their face.

GeneDef.label: fat body
GeneDef.description: Carriers can have fat bodies. A person can have more than one body type gene; one body type will be chosen among those that are allowed.

GeneDef.label: thin body
GeneDef.description: Carriers can have thin bodies. A person can have more than one body type gene; one body type will be chosen among those that are allowed.

GeneDef.label: hulk body
GeneDef.description: Carriers can have large bodies. A person can have more than one body type gene; one body type will be chosen among those that are allowed.

GeneDef.label: standard body
GeneDef.description: Carriers can have average-shaped bodies. A person can have more than one body type gene; one body type will be chosen among those that are allowed.

GeneDef.label: human ears
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regular human ears.

GeneDef.label: pig ears
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene will grow pointed pig-like ears.

GeneDef.label: floppy ears
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow long, floppy hound-like ears.

GeneDef.label: cat ears
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have cat-like ears.

GeneDef.label: pointed ears
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have pointed ears.

GeneDef.label: human nose
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regular human noses.

GeneDef.label: pig nose
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have pig-like snouts.

GeneDef.label: human jaw
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regularly-shaped jaws.

GeneDef.label: heavy jaw
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have large jaws.

GeneDef.label: gaunt head
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a pinched, gaunt appearance in their face and head.

GeneDef.label: human hands
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regular human hands.

GeneDef.label: trotter hands
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have hands that partially resemble pig trotters. This reduces their ability to manipulate objects.

GeneDef.label: elongated fingers
GeneDef.description: Long, delicate fingers improve the carrier's manipulation capacity. This aids with many tasks, especially crafting and construction.

GeneDef.label: human headbone
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regular human skulls.

GeneDef.label: mini-horns
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow two small horns protruding from the forehead.

GeneDef.label: center-horn
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow a single horn protruding from the center of the forehead.

GeneDef.label: human voice
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have regular human vocal cords.

GeneDef.label: pig voice
GeneDef.description: Carriers have a squealing voice like that of a pig.

GeneDef.label: roar voice
GeneDef.description: Carriers have an animal-like roaring voice.

GeneDef.label: slow wound healing
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene heal from wounds half as fast as normal.

GeneDef.label: fast wound healing
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene heal from wounds twice as fast as normal.

GeneDef.label: superfast wound healing
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene heal from wounds four times as fast as normal.

GeneDef.label: weak immunity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene gain immunity to diseases more slowly than normal. They may die from infections that others would survive.

GeneDef.label: strong immunity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene gain immunity to diseases faster than normal.

GeneDef.label: super immunity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene gain immunity to diseases considerably faster than normal.

GeneDef.label: partial antitoxic lungs
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are resistant to environmental toxins. They get less toxic buildup from tox gas, polluted terrain, and toxic fallout, but are still vulnerable to direct attacks with venom or injected poison. Additionally, they build up rot stink exposure slower.

GeneDef.label: total antitoxic lungs
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are immune to environmental toxins, but not from direct toxic attacks. They get no toxic buildup from tox gas, polluted terrain, or toxic fallout, and they are not bothered by acidic smog. They are still vulnerable to direct attacks like venom and injected poison. Additionally, they are immune to rot stink exposure.

GeneDef.label: sterile
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene cannot reproduce by natural means.

GeneDef.label: fertile
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a higher chance of becoming pregnant or impregnating others.

GeneDef.label: superclotting
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have extra-power coagulating factors in their blood, and will stop bleeding very quickly when wounded.

GeneDef.label: kind instinct
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are high in trait agreeableness and are very conscientious. They rarely insult others and will sometimes offer kind words to brighten the moods of those around them. They also never judge people by their appearance.

GeneDef.label: violence disabled
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are emotionally and mentally incapable of engaging in violence. They are overwhelmingly resistant to and horrified by the idea of hurting another.

GeneDef.label: nearsighted
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have difficulty seeing at a distance. Their shooting accuracy at long ranges is reduced.

GeneDef.label: strong stomach
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have an extra toxin-filtering organ in their stomach and will never suffer from food poisoning even after eating rotten food.

GeneDef.label: dark vision
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene see well in low light and are unaffected by mood penalties related to darkness. They have a reflective layer behind the retina that amplifies their ability to see in the dark.

GeneDef.label: indoor dweller
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have no need for the outdoors and will never feel cooped up no matter how long they stay inside.

GeneDef.label: kill thirst
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene lust for the feeling of ending another's life. They will become irritated if they go for too long without killing someone in close combat.

GeneDef.label: fire resistant
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have special fast-acting sweat glands and heat-resistant skin. They only take 25% of the normal damage from fire. The chance of them catching on fire is also drastically reduced.

GeneDef.label: inbred
GeneDef.description: This genetic condition affects a person's fertility, immunity, and mental capacity.

GeneDef.label: robust digestion
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene grow a multi-fold stomach, allowing them to digest raw foods more efficiently than baseline humans. In general, they get the same nutrition from raw food as from if it is cooked. They also don't mind the taste of raw food at all.

GeneDef.label: mild cell instability
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene need less metabolic energy to stay alive, at the cost of reduced stability in their cell-replication machinery.

GeneDef.label: major cell instability
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene need much less metabolic energy to stay alive, at the cost of greatly-reduced stability in their cell-replication machinery.

GeneDef.label: psychic bonding
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a special neural organ that makes them psychically bond with a lover for life. As long as the lovers are together, they will be happy. If they are physically separated, they will be disturbed by the distance. If one dies, the other's mind will be badly disrupted.

customEffectDescriptions.li: Gains psychic bond with first romantic partner.

GeneDef.label: pollution stimulus
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene get a chemical rush from being exposed to pollution. This makes them move faster and helps them think clearer. A similar gene is found in combat-engineered mega-insects.

customEffectDescriptions.li: Gain stat bonuses when exposed to pollution.

GeneDef.label: unstoppable
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are not slowed down when taking damage.

GeneDef.label: naked speed
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene move slower while clothed, and faster while naked.

GeneDef.label: webbed phalanges
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have webbed fingers and toes, allowing them to move faster in water. Webbed fingers slightly reduce fine motor control.

GeneDef.label: hemogenic
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a reserve of biological strength powered by a resource called hemogen. The resource can be gained and spent in various ways, all of which are unlocked by other genes.\n\nCarriers lose 2 hemogen per day from biological entropy.
GeneDef.resourceDescription:
A reserve of biological strength which can be gained and spent in a variety of ways.

Hemogen can be increased by bloodfeeding from a human or consuming hemogen packs. You can obtain hemogen packs using the 'extract hemogen pack' medical operation on a non-hemogenic human.

If hemogen reaches zero, {PAWN_nameDef} will become very unhappy.

GeneDef.label: hemogen drain
GeneDef.description: Carriers lose an additional 8 hemogen per day from biological entropy.

GeneDef.label: tinderskin
GeneDef.description: Carriers have dry, thin skin which burns easily from fire, and their immune systems react very poorly to this kind of threat. Damage from fire is multiplied by 4.

GeneDef.label: pyrophobia
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have an intense fear of fire. When fires are close, there is a chance they will have a mental breakdown at any moment.

customEffectDescriptions.li: May have a mental breakdown when near fires.

li.label: afraid of fire
li.description: The flames make me so nervous. Such searing heat - I feel like it will leap at me at any moment!

GeneDef.label: perfect immunity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have archite-enhanced immune systems which intelligently destroy invaders. They are totally immune to most normal illnesses.

GeneDef.label: non-senescent
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene do not go through senescence in the normal way. They never get chronic age-related diseases like cancer, bad back, cataracts, or dementia.

GeneDef.label: scarless
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a special type of regenerator cell which can heal old wounds and chronic illnesses like bad back.

customEffectDescriptions.li: Every (*DateTime)15-30 days(/DateTime), one old wound or chronic illness is healed.

GeneDef.label: deathrest
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene must periodically regenerate themselves in a special coma called deathrest. Deathrest takes days, but can confer substantial bonuses. Deathrest can be accelerated and its effects enhanced by the use of a variety of special buildings and technologies.\n\nThose who put off deathresting will suffer from deathrest exhaustion.

GeneDef.label: ageless
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have archites in the bloodstream which continuously reverse the process of aging. Starting at the age of 13, carriers begin to biologically age slower. By 18, the aging process stops completely.

GeneDef.label: deathless
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have archites in the blood which will sustain their life processes no matter what. As long as the brain remains intact, a carrier of this gene will never die.

customEffectDescriptions.li: Can only die from destruction of brain.

GeneDef.label: archite metabolism
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have special archites in their cells that facilitate and optimize metabolism. This improves overall genetic and metabolic quality.

GeneDef.label: cold weakness
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly less comfortable in cold temperatures.

GeneDef.label: cold tolerant
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly more comfortable in cold temperatures.

GeneDef.label: cold super-tolerant
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are much more comfortable in cold temperatures.

GeneDef.label: heat super-tolerant
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are more comfortable in warm temperatures.

GeneDef.label: heat tolerant
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly more comfortable in warm temperatures.

GeneDef.label: heat weakness
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly less comfortable in warm temperatures.

GeneDef.label: psychically deaf
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are deaf to all psychic energy and influence outside their own minds. They cannot be affected by psychic influence, nor can they ever wield psychic power.

GeneDef.label: psychically dull
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are less psychically-sensitive than others.

GeneDef.label: psy-sensitive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are more psychically-sensitive than average.

GeneDef.label: super psy-sensitive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are much more psychically-sensitive than most.

GeneDef.label: slow runner
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene move more slowly than normal.

GeneDef.label: fast runner
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene move more quickly than normal.

GeneDef.label: very fast runner
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene move much more quickly than normal.

GeneDef.label: very unattractive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have misshapen, asymmetrical facial structures and blotchy skin. They're hard to look at.

GeneDef.label: unattractive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have exaggerated facial features and poor skin that are generally considered ugly.

GeneDef.label: attractive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have unusually symmetrical, balanced facial features and extra-clear skin which gives them a pleasing appearance.

GeneDef.label: very attractive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have remarkably precise and symmetrical faces. Their features are distinctive and strong without being exaggerated, and their skin is nearly perfect. They are generally seen as beautiful.

GeneDef.label: slow study
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have deficient long-term memories and don't understand new ideas quickly. They are slow at learning new skills and knowledge.

GeneDef.label: quick study
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have excellent memories and grasp new ideas quickly. They learn faster than others.

GeneDef.label: very unhappy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are highly predisposed to negative emotion. They'll see the bad in every situation and have a much lower mood than others.

GeneDef.label: unhappy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are predisposed to pessimistic perceptions. They'll tend to interpret things negatively and have lower mood than others.

GeneDef.label: happy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are predisposed to optimistic feelings. They'll have higher mood than others.

GeneDef.label: very happy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are highly predisposed to optimism and not at all inclined to think negatively. They'll have much higher mood than others.

GeneDef.label: tox resistance
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are resistant to toxic buildup from any source. This includes pollution, toxic fallout, tox gas, and direct attacks with venom or injected poison. They'll gain half the amount of toxic buildup compared to others.\n\nCellular filters in the lung and skin reduce the dose of toxins entering the bloodstream.

GeneDef.label: tox immunity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are totally immune to toxic buildup from all sources including polluted terrain, toxic fallout, tox gas, and direct attacks with venom or injected poison. They are also not bothered by acidic smog.\n\nThe carrier's biochemical pathways are modified to route around interference from nearly all known toxins. Along with enhancements to the kidneys and liver, this keeps carriers comfortable in even the most toxic of environments.

GeneDef.label: delicate
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene take greater injuries than others from the same damage. They have thin, brittle bones and less binding molecules in joints and flesh.

GeneDef.label: robust
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene take less injuries than others from the same damage. They have thickened, densified bones, nearly-solid ribcages, and strengthened binding factors in joints and flesh.

GeneDef.label: reduced pain
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene feel half as much pain compared to a baseliner. Reduced neuron activity in the brain's nociception centers makes pain dull and faint. This can be advantageous sometimes, and dangerous other times.

GeneDef.label: extra pain
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene feel more pain than others given the same injuries. Neuron activity in the brain's nociception center is amplified, so pain feels extra-intense and fiery. This can be protective, but overall it's considered a negative and makes it hard to push through difficult situations.

GeneDef.label: dead calm
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene feel calm in every situation and have a very placid demeanor. They will never start social fights or have aggressive mental breaks.

GeneDef.label: aggressive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are quick to anger. They are twice as likely to start social fights. When they have mental breaks, they are twice as likely to choose an aggressive kind of break.

GeneDef.label: hyper-aggressive
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are hormonally high-strung and very aggressive. They are three times as likely to start social fights. Any mental break they have will be of an aggressive type.

GeneDef.label: very sleepy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene get tired much faster than others.

GeneDef.label: sleepy
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene get tired somewhat faster than others.

GeneDef.label: low sleep
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene get tired less quickly than others.

GeneDef.label: never sleep
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have a unique metabolic process which allows clusters of neurons to sleep while the rest of the brain stays awake. They never need to sleep.

GeneDef.label: weak melee damage
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene do less damage in close-quarters combat. Weak fast-twitch muscle fibers make their strikes shaky and weak.

GeneDef.label: strong melee damage
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene do more damage in close-quarters combat. Extra-strong fast-twitch muscle fibers make their strikes accurate and powerful.

GeneDef.label: mild UV sensitivity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have biological compounds in their skin that react painfully to UV radiation. They are unusually sensitive to sunlight.

GeneDef.label: intense UV sensitivity
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene have biological compounds in their skin that react dangerously to UV radiation. They are intensely sensitive to sunlight.

GeneDef.label: low libido
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are less likely to engage in lovin' with their partner.

GeneDef.label: high libido
GeneDef.description: Carriers of this gene are more likely to engage in lovin' with their partner.

GeneTemplateDef.label: awful {0}
GeneTemplateDef.description: The carrier's aptitude in {0} is reduced by 8. Aptitude acts like an offset on skill level. Additionally, all passion is removed from {0}.

GeneTemplateDef.label: poor {0}
GeneTemplateDef.description: The carrier's aptitude in {0} is reduced by 4. Aptitude acts like an offset on skill level.

GeneTemplateDef.label: strong {0}
GeneTemplateDef.description: The carrier's aptitude in {0} is increased by 4. Aptitude acts like an offset on skill level.

GeneTemplateDef.label: great {0}
GeneTemplateDef.description: The carrier's aptitude in {0} is increased by 8. Aptitude acts like an offset on skill level. Additionally, one level of passion is added to {0}.

GeneTemplateDef.label: {0} dependency
GeneTemplateDef.description: Carriers of this gene need to ingest {0} on a regular basis to survive. After {DEFICIENCYDURATION} without {0}, carriers will suffer from {0} deficiency. After {COMADURATION}, they will fall into a coma. After {DEATHDURATION}, they will die.

GeneTemplateDef.label: {0} resistant
GeneTemplateDef.description: Carriers are only half as likely to become addicted to {0}.

GeneTemplateDef.label: {0} impervious
