While growing or gestating, the vat must be fed with a constant supply of nutrition to provide the feedstock for growth. Gestating an embryo takes twice the nutrition of accelerating a child's growth.

Embryos are gestated for 9 days before a baby is formed. There is a risk of health complications.

Child growth can only be accelerated up to age 18, but not beyond. While growing, a child's skills will slowly increase. Children raised in growth vats will have lower skills and gain fewer passions than normal.

The device uses chemical injections, electrical stimulation, and simple mechanite treatments to push the body to grow. Growth vats are often used to quickly manufacture engineered workers or warriors.

ThingDef.label: mechband antenna
ThingDef.description: A mech-band signaling device. When activated, it puts out a powerful mech signal pulse, which will attract an ultra-heavy feral mechanoid to attack with its escorts. If you can defeat it, you can collect special technologies from its corpse. The signal pulse burns out the transmitter, so this building can only be used once.

ThingDef.label: mechband dish
ThingDef.description: A mech-band signaling device more powerful than the normal mechband antenna. When activated, it puts out an ultra-powerful mech signal pulse, which will attract a mechanoid commander to attack with its escorts. If you can defeat it, you can collect special technologies from its corpse. The signal pulse burns out the dish, so this building can only be used once.

ThingDef.label: pollution pump
ThingDef.description: A groundwater-filtering pump which slowly cleans polluted terrain. The extracted pollution is formed into toxic wastepacks which must be hauled away.

ThingDef.label: crashed mechanitor ship
ThingDef.description: A short-range ship used by a mechanitor to transport mechs for low-orbit or planetary travel.

ThingDef.label: wastepack atomizer
ThingDef.description: A glittertech device that deconstructs toxic wastepacks into inert gases using advanced molecular processes. The process requires considerable amounts of power.

ThingDef.label: blood torch
ThingDef.description: A specially-treated wooden torch that produces a red light over a large area. Sanguophages gather around torches like these during their ceremonial meetings. The sanguine glow is particularly pleasing to individuals with the bloodfeeder gene. It can be automatically refueled with wood, and produces a small amount of heat.

ThingDef.label: gene processor
ThingDef.description: A genetic analysis and processing system. Placed near a gene assembler, it increases the maximum genetic complexity of the xenogerms you can assemble. Building multiple gene processors will increase the genetic complexity limit further.

HediffDef.label: mechanoid boost
HediffDef.description: This mechanoid's capacities have been boosted by a nearby mechanoid booster building.

ThingDef.label: mech booster
ThingDef.description: A remote energy and computation enhancement device. Any friendly mechanoids in its effect radius will move and work faster.

ThingDef.label: IED tox trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of tox gas shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: mech gestator
ThingDef.description: A tank of mechanite-rich fluid with support tubes for feeding in materials and nutrients. Mechanitors can use it to produce new mechanoids or to resurrect dead mechanoids. This basic type of mech gestator is only capable of generating light-weight mechs.\n\nThe process uses harsh chemicals which are stored in toxic wastepacks. Haulers must remove the wastepacks from time to time.

ThingDef.label: large mech gestator
ThingDef.description: A tank of mechanite-rich fluid with support tubes for feeding in materials and nutrients. Mechanitors can use it to produce new mechanoids or to resurrect dead mechanoids. This tier of mech gestator is capable of generating medium, heavy, and ultraheavy mechs.\n\nThe process uses harsh chemicals which are stored in toxic wastepacks. Haulers must remove the wastepacks from time to time.

ThingDef.label: subcore encoder
ThingDef.description: A work station where a mechanitor can produce basic-tier subcores. Subcores are the brains of mechanoids, and one is required to produce any mechanoid. Basic subcores can only be used in simple basic-tier mechs.\n\nHigher tier subcores can be created by building a subcore softscanner or a subcore ripscanner.

ThingDef.label: subcore softscanner
ThingDef.description:
A pod with thousands of tiny tissue probes and a high-energy brain scanner. Once a person is inserted, the system uses the probes and scanner to sense a neuro-psychic pattern that it can analog-transfer to a new standard-tier mechanoid subcore. The person will be left temporarily sick, but unharmed.

Subcores are mechanoid brains and producing any mechanoid requires one. Standard-tier subcores produced by this softscanner can only power standard-tier mechanoids.

Higher tier subcores can be created by building a subcore ripscanner.

ThingDef.label: subcore ripscanner
ThingDef.description: A pod with thousands of tissue probe injectors and an ultra-high-power vaporizing brain scanner. Once a person is inserted, the device will insert the probes into their body through the skin while the ripscanner chews through the brain, reading the reflected radiation and destroying the brain in the process. Ripscanning the mind generates a neuro-psychic pattern that the scanner can analog-transfer to a new high-tier mechanoid subcore.\n\nSubcores are mechanoid brains and producing any mechanoid requires one. High-tier subcores produced by this ripscanner can only power high-tier mechanoids.

ThingDef.label: mech recharger
ThingDef.description: Lightweight mechanoids can recharge here. During recharge, this recharger produces toxic wastepacks and stores them internally. Haulers must remove the wastepacks from time to time.

ThingDef.label: large mech recharger
ThingDef.description: Medium, heavy, and ultraheavy mechanoids can recharge here. During recharge, this recharger produces toxic wastepacks and stores them internally. Haulers must remove the wastepacks from time to time.

ThingDef.label: baby food
ThingDef.description: A bland vegetarian mash. Babies love it, but children and adults will be upset if they're forced to eat it.

ThingDef.label: hemogen pack
ThingDef.description: A package of refined hemogen in a specialized container that prevents spoilage. Hemogenic humans can consume it to restore their internal hemogen stores. It can be administered via an operation to reverse blood loss.

ThingDef.label: basic subcore
ThingDef.description: The simplest possible mechanoid brain, this is a tiny psychodynamic substrate unit housing a dull subpersona. Since this is only a basic-tier subcore, it can only drive the simplest of mechanoids.\n\nLike all mechanoid subcores, it contains a subpersona with a psychic presence, albeit a very faint one.

ThingDef.label: standard subcore
ThingDef.description: A standard-tier mechanoid brain, this is a psychodynamic substrate unit supporting a thinking subpersona. This particular subcore is strong enough to drive standard-tier mechanoids.\n\nMechanoids are more than robots, and this is more than a silicon computer. Its thinking, psychically-present subpersona makes it more adaptable than silicon systems. However, this also means it can only be produced by analog pattern transfer from another thinking mind.

ThingDef.label: high subcore
ThingDef.description:
A high-tier mechanoid brain, this is a psychodynamic substrate unit which supports a sophisticated subpersona. This particular subcore is of the strongest tier, and can power complex ultra-heavy mechanoids.

The subpersona inside this core approaches a live human in its complexity, though it is of a very different nature. Like any such mind, it has a noticeable psychic presence.

This subcore could only have been produced by rich pattern transfer from another sophisticated mind. The only way to do this without huge facilities is to ripscan a living person's brain, killing them in the process.

ThingDef.label: signal chip
ThingDef.description: A mechanoid-band synchronization micro-organ. It is necessary to produce certain advanced types of mechanoids and equipment.\n\nA mechanitor can study this chip to help unlock higher tiers of mechtech research.

li.completedLetter: By studying the signal chip, {PAWN_labelShort} has acquired the insight needed for the research project(s) {RESEARCH}.\n\nYour researchers can now use research benches to begin researching how to actually use the technology.
li.inspectString: Can be analyzed by a colonist.

ThingDef.label: powerfocus chip
ThingDef.description: An energy-focusing mechanoid micro-organ. It is necessary to produce certain advanced types of mechanoids and equipment.\n\nA mechanitor can study this chip to help unlock higher tiers of mechtech research.

li.completedLetter: By studying the powerfocus chip, {PAWN_labelShort} has acquired the insight needed for the research project(s) {RESEARCH}.\n\nYour researchers can now use research benches to begin researching how to actually use the technology.
li.inspectString: Can be analyzed by a colonist.

ThingDef.label: nano structuring chip
ThingDef.description: A molecular-restructing mechanoid micro-organ. It is necessary to produce certain advanced mechanoids and equipment.\n\nA mechanitor can study this chip to help unlock higher tiers of mechtech research.

li.completedLetter: By studying the nano structuring chip, {PAWN_labelShort} has acquired the insight needed for the research project(s) {RESEARCH}.\n\nYour researchers can now use research benches to begin researching how to actually use the technology.
li.inspectString: Can be analyzed by a colonist.

ThingDef.label: deathrest capacity serum
ThingDef.description: A serum that permanently increases the number of deathrest buildings a person can connect to during deathrest.\n\nThe serum can only be ingested by individuals with the deathrest gene.

ThingDef.label: toxic wastepack
ThingDef.description: A compacted package of toxic waste that will slowly dissolve if not frozen. The surface is heat-sealed for safe transport. Wastepacks will pollute the surrounding terrain if they dissolve, deteriorate, or are otherwise destroyed.\n\nToxic wastepacks are flammable. If burned or damaged, they will release tox gas.

ThingDef.label: tox shell
ThingDef.description: An artillery shell containing reagents that, when combined, generate deadly tox gas. When fired, it will stick into the ground and release tox gas for some time before expiring.\n\nTox gas burns the lungs and eyes, causing a temporary shortness of breath and reduction in sight. Continued exposure to tox gas results in toxic buildup that can be lethal.

ThingDef.label: toxipotatoes
ThingDef.description: Raw toxipotatoes. Once harvested, toxipotatoes are very dietarily similar to potatoes. However, when eaten raw, they have a higher chance of causing food poisoning.

ThingDef.label: unfinished subcore
ThingDef.description: An unfinished mechanoid subcore.

ThingDef.label: genepack
ThingDef.description: A small capsule containing a package of genetic information. To use a genepack, it must be placed in a gene bank near a gene assembler and combined into an implantable xenogerm.\n\nIf not kept in a powered gene bank, this genepack will slowly deteriorate.

ThingDef.label: xenogerm
ThingDef.description:
A self-contained biological organ containing one or more implantable xenogenes.

Once implanted inside a host's body, the xenogerm modifies the host's genes, gene expression, and phenotypic development using viruses, hormones, bio-synthesized drugs, and possibly mechanites. Depending on the xenogerm, the host will develop any of a wide variety of exotic traits and abilities, transforming them into a different human xenotype.

Xenogerm implantation is a traumatic process. Once implanted with a xenogerm, a person will be bedridden for days as the transformation sets in.

During storage and transport, xenogerms are kept safe in sealed containers.

ThingDef.label: archite capsule
ThingDef.description: A small capsule containing archites - microscopic machines produced by a superintelligent archotech. These devices are capable of physical and psychic feats which seem impossible to human scientists. As with all archotechnology, no human can create one. We can only try to scavenge the ones that archotechs create for their own unfathomable reasons.\n\nThis capsule is useless by itself, but it can be spent at a gene assembler to create a new archite-powered xenogerm. This requires researching archogenetics and a genepack that contains an archite gene. Archite genepacks can be obtained from traders.

ThingDef.label: mechanoid transponder
ThingDef.description: A transponder micro-organ that connects a mechanitor to a mechanoid, even over a great distance. Mechanitors are capable of controlling many mechanoids using a mix of psychic and electromagnetic signals.\n\nDecrypting the transponder will allow you to pinpoint the location of the last mechanitor who controlled the mechanoid.

li.inspectString: Can be decrypted at a research bench.\nSelect a colonist and right-click this to decrypt it.

ThingDef.label: ovum
ThingDef.description: An extracted, unfertilized human ovum cell stored in a protective capsule. Once fertilized by a male, it becomes an embryo which can then be implanted into a human mother or growth vat.

ThingDef.label: embryo
ThingDef.description: A human embryo which can be implanted in a mother to create a pregnancy.

ThingDef.label: kid romper
ThingDef.description: A combined t-shirt and pants sized for kids, with a snuggly built-in undergarment. Little ones love it!

ThingDef.label: kid shirt
ThingDef.description: A small, simple t-shirt sized to fit children.

ThingDef.label: kid pants
ThingDef.description: A small set of pants sized to fit children.

ThingDef.label: kid parka
ThingDef.description: A heavy jacket for keeping a child warm in cold temperatures.

ThingDef.label: kid tribalwear
ThingDef.description: A one-piece garment sized for kids, crafted using neolithic tools. It provides effective insulation against the elements.

ThingDef.label: kid helmet
ThingDef.description: A simple helmet sized for children. It gives moderate protection against sharp attacks. Not effective against blunt weapons. That said, if this is being used in combat something has already gone very wrong.

ThingDef.label: airwire headset
ThingDef.description: A simple head-mounted comms computer that slightly enhances a mechanitor's control bandwidth. This allows them to control more mechs.

ThingDef.label: array headset
ThingDef.description: A head-mounted computer and signaling array that enhances a mechanitor's control bandwidth. This allows them to control more mechs.

ThingDef.label: integrator headset
ThingDef.description: An advanced head-mounted computer and signaling array that dramatically enhances a mechanitor's control bandwidth. This allows the wearer to control many more mechanoids at once.

ThingDef.label: mechcommander helmet
ThingDef.description: A plasteel-weave combat helmet designed for battle mechanitors. It is embedded with computers and signal enhancers that moderately increase the wearer's maximum control bandwidth. This allows the mechanitor to control more mechs.

ThingDef.label: mechlord helmet
ThingDef.description: A heavy plasteel-weave helmet packed with mechanitor-assistance gear. The mechlord helmet dramatically amplifies a mechanitor's bandwidth, but is somewhat less protective than dedicated heavy armor.

ThingDef.label: gas mask
ThingDef.description: A flexible mask worn over the face with an embedded air filter. It dramatically reduces exposure to pollution through the lungs, but does not protect the skin on the rest of the body.\n\nIt prevents tox gas irritants from entering through the eyes and mouth.

ThingDef.label: heavy shield unit
ThingDef.description: A mechanoid-built projectile-repulsion device. The user can shoot out, but the shield will block shots coming in. This shield only protects the user, not those around them. It does nothing against melee attacks or heat. The shield will break instantly if hit by EMP.

ThingDef.label: control pack
ThingDef.description: A backpack containing mech control assist computers. It allows a mechanitor to control one additional control group.

ThingDef.label: bandwidth pack
ThingDef.description: A backpack containing bandwidth-expansion computer and antenna. It can increase a mechanitor's maximum total bandwidth.

ThingDef.label: tox pack
ThingDef.description:
A reusable backpack containing canisters of reagents and a mechanism that uses them to generate tox gas. When the wearer activates the pack, it will begin spreading tox gas and continue for several seconds until it runs out of reagents.

Once used, it must be reloaded with chemfuel before it can be used again.

Tox gas burns the lungs and eyes, causing a temporary shortness of breath and reduction in sight. Continued exposure to tox gas results in toxic buildup which can be lethal.

ThingDef.label: mechlord suit
ThingDef.description: A power-assisted armor suit packed with mechanitor-assistance gear. The mechlord suit dramatically amplifies a mechanitor's bandwidth, but is somewhat less protective than dedicated heavy armor.

ThingDef.label: heavy bandolier
ThingDef.description: A heavy shoulder-belt for keeping spare munitions close at hand. It allows quick access to bullets, grenades, arrows, or whatever the user needs, reducing their weapon's ranged cooldown. Due to its bulk, it can't be worn under other clothing. It doesn't cover the body, so it can be worn happily by nudists and yttakin.

ThingDef.label: sash
ThingDef.description: A long strip of material worn over one shoulder. It offers minimal protection from heat, cold, and attacks. Due to its minimalist nature, nudists won't complain about wearing it.

ThingDef.label: mechanitor ship (crashing)
ThingDef.description: A short-range ship used by a mechanitor to transport mechs for low-orbit or planetary travel.

ThingDef.label: toxbomb launcher
ThingDef.description: A self-loading low-pressure canister launcher loaded with tox bombs. Upon impact, the tox bombs will stick to the ground and release tox gas for several seconds.\n\nTox gas burns the lungs and eyes, causing a temporary shortness of breath and reduction in sight. Continued exposure to tox gas results in toxic buildup which can be lethal.

ThingDef.label: tox grenades
ThingDef.description: Grenades loaded with liquified tox gas. Upon landing, they stick to the ground and release tox gas for several seconds.\n\nTox gas burns the lungs and eyes, causing a temporary shortness of breath and reduction in sight. Continued exposure to tox gas results in toxic buildup which can be lethal.

ThingDef.label: flamebow
ThingDef.description: A simple short selfbow with a load of incendiary arrows. The arrows carry fuel and an igniter. Upon impact, they spray fuel around and ignite it.

ThingDef.label: hellsphere cannon
ThingDef.description: A ultra-high-power energy pulse projector designed for siegebreaking. The hellsphere cannon must hold a bead on its target for several seconds while charging, before it releases a devastating tsunami of power. The explosion is capable of melting concrete in its blast radius. The heat of the explosion will ignite anything nearby. It cannot fire at close-up targets.

ThingDef.label: mini-shotgun
ThingDef.description: A compact, short-range shotgun designed to be mounted on a light combat mechanoid.

ThingDef.label: slugthrower
ThingDef.description: A compact single-shot slug thrower designed to be mounted on a light combat mechanoid.

ThingDef.label: spiner
ThingDef.description: A very small gun used by war urchins which quickly fires spine-like projectiles. It is short-ranged but deadly.

ThingDef.label: mini-flameblaster
ThingDef.description: A small burst-oriented flamethrower used by mechanoids.

ThingDef.label: beam graser
ThingDef.description: A gamma ray laser which fires a sweeping beam. The narrow, high-energy beam can pierce thick armor and ignite targets.

ThingDef.label: toxic needle gun
ThingDef.description: A mechanoid-built gun that fires toxin-infused metal needles. It can fire long distances and will poison the target in addition to doing physical damage.

ThingDef.label: needle launcher
ThingDef.description: This mechanoid weapon is a compact version of the needle gun. Named after its needle-like projectiles, it fires single shots with great accuracy. The needle launcher has less range than its counterpart but is lightweight, allowing it to be wielded by fast-moving mechs.

ThingDef.label: toxipotato plant
ThingDef.description: A genetically-engineered variant of potato adapted for growing in polluted areas. Compared to regular potatoes, toxipotatoes take less time to grow but yield a meager harvest of food. When eaten raw, they have a high chance of causing food poisoning. In spite of this, they have saved many settlers from starvation after toxic events.

ThingDef.label: polux tree
ThingDef.description: After generations of exposure, these trees have evolved to metabolize pollutants. By drawing pollutants from the ground through wide root networks, they slowly clean polluted terrain in their vicinity. However, they cannot do this if buildings are constructed over their roots.\n\nUnlike most methods of cleaning polluted terrain, polux trees do not create toxic wastepacks.

ThingDef.label: chopped polux stump
ThingDef.description: A stump left behind after a polux tree has been felled. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.label: smashed polux stump
ThingDef.description: The remnants of a polux tree destroyed by damage. It's ugly. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.label: polux seed
ThingDef.description: The seed of a polux tree. It can be planted to create a new polux tree which will absorb pollution from nearby terrain.

ThingDef.label: gray grass
ThingDef.description: Gray grass refers to a variety of species of wild toxin-adapted grass. It grows anywhere there is minimally-fertile polluted ground and the climate isn't overwhelming hostile.

ThingDef.label: ripthorn
ThingDef.description: A short toxin-adapted shrub that looks like a dense, tough tangle of thorny branches. Difficult to move through, it slows down anyone moving over it. It can only grow in polluted areas.

ThingDef.label: pebble cactus
ThingDef.description: A small cactus that resembles a cluster of pebbles. It can only grow on polluted terrain. It yields a meager amount of woody fiber when harvested.

ThingDef.label: gray pine tree
ThingDef.description: A small toxin-adapted tree with twisted branches. It can only grow on polluted terrain, and yields a meager amount of wood when harvested.

ThingDef.label: witchwood tree
ThingDef.description: A small toxin-adapted tree with a twisted trunk. It can only grow on polluted terrain. When harvested, it yields a meager amount of wood.

ThingDef.label: rat palm tree
ThingDef.description: A tree similar to a palm tree with dense surface roots. It can only grow on polluted terrain. When harvested, it yields a meager amount of wood.

ThingDef.label: chopped stump
ThingDef.description: A stump left behind after a polluted tree has been felled. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.label: smashed stump
ThingDef.description: The remnants of a polluted tree destroyed by damage. It's ugly. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.label: waste rat
ThingDef.description: A toxin-adapted variant of the common rat. Waste rats have evolved to be pollution-resistant, as well as larger, tougher, and more aggressive than standard rats. Their bite infects their attacker with toxic buildup.

ThingDef.label: toxalope
ThingDef.description: A pollution-adapted cousin of the boomalope, the toxalope grows toxic pouches on its back. When it dies, the toxic material explodes and produces a deadly toxic cloud. Unlike the boomalope, the toxalope cannot be milked.

ThingDef.label: tunneler
ThingDef.description: A heavy mechanoid built for mining in treacherous locations. While intended for excavation, the tunneler's gigantic power claws and ultra-thick armor makes it a dangerous force in combat.

ThingDef.label: militor
ThingDef.description: A small combat mechanoid armed with a low-power mini-shotgun. Roughly four feet tall, militors lack the power, range, and toughness of more senior combat mechs. However, it is cheap to gestate and maintain, and so is often used as a rear guard or swarm attacker.\n\nIn war, mech armies are known to send militors into urban ruins to hunt down survivors after breaking the human defenses. For this reason, they are considered by some to be the most cruel of all mechanoid patterns.

ThingDef.label: lifter
ThingDef.description: A small mechanoid designed for hauling. Lacking a ranged weapon, it can make only weak melee attacks.

ThingDef.label: constructoid
ThingDef.description: A small mechanoid designed to perform construction tasks. It can perform blunt melee attacks if necessary.

ThingDef.label: fabricor
ThingDef.description: A small work mechanoid designed to craft all manner of manufactured objects.

ThingDef.label: agrihand
ThingDef.description: A small mechanoid designed to sow and harvest crops. While it is better suited to labor than combat, it can fight with built-in cutting blades if necessary.

ThingDef.label: cleansweeper
ThingDef.description: A light mechanoid designed for cleaning. Lacking a ranged weapon, it can make only weak melee attacks.

ThingDef.label: war urchin
ThingDef.description: A small, deployable combat mechanoid usually manufactured inside an ultra-heavy war queen mech. War urchins are expendable fighters designed to swarm-attack enemies. They are mounted with short-ranged spiner guns and have a non-rechargeable power source.

ThingDef.label: paramedic
ThingDef.description: A small mechanoid designed for non-violent emergency situation management and medical care. The paramedic can rescue the wounded, fight fires, treat the sick, and even perform surgery when a more-qualified human is not available. Its built-in jump launcher allows it to jump into, and out of, emergency situations, and its built-in firefoam popper can quickly extinguish fires.

ThingDef.label: legionary
ThingDef.description: A combat support mechanoid with a wide-range bullet shield and mid-range needle gun. Designed to support other mechanoids, the legionary is vulnerable to anyone who can get inside its shield.

ThingDef.label: tesseron
ThingDef.description: A medium-range combat mechanoid. While it is fairly vulnerable to attacks, the tesseron's sweeping beam graser can pierce thick armor and even ignite shielded targets.

ThingDef.label: scorcher
ThingDef.description: A close-approach war mechanoid that specializes in incendiary attacks. Its flame burst attack has little reach, but once it closes on a group of defenders it can ignite and disrupt them with blasts of searing flame.

ThingDef.label: apocriton
ThingDef.description: A mechanoid commander designed to coordinate and motivate other mechs during long extermination campaigns. Its most obvious power is its ability to resurrect recently-killed mechs by supercharging their self-repair processes. Less obviously, it is intelligent and psychically present, radiating hatred into the minds of anyone in a wide radius. It can also move quickly with its built-in jump launcher.\n\nWhile all mechanoids have a dim psychically-present intelligence, only the apocriton and a few others truly feel hatred for their victims and understand the suffering they inflict.

ThingDef.Name: MechCenturion
ThingDef.label: centurion
ThingDef.description: An ultraheavy mech with a built-in shield bubble generator. The centurion carries a point-defense bulb turret capable of firing while the mechanoid is moving.

ThingDef.label: charge blaster turret
ThingDef.description: A small charge blaster designed for use on a defense turret.

ThingDef.Name: MechWarqueen
ThingDef.label: war queen
ThingDef.description: An ultra-heavy mech with a built-in mech gestator. Fed with appropriate resources, the war queen can form small war urchin combat mechs within its massive carapace and deploy them into combat.\n\nEven more than other mechanoids, the war queen resembles a giant, living insect. All war mechs can be terrifying, but humans tend to find the war queen disturbing on a deeper level.

ThingDef.Name: MechDiabolus
ThingDef.label: diabolus
ThingDef.description: An ultra-heavy mechanoid with an ultra-powerful hellsphere cannon. Made for siegebreaking, its hellsphere cannon takes time to charge up a shot, but can melt concrete and vaporize bone. The diabolus dissipates the hellsphere cannon's waste power in a heat column mounted on its back, which can pulse to ignite flammable objects nearby.\n\nThis mech's name comes from a thousand-year-old poem written by a Haspian monk who survived the erasure of his monastery. His religiously-tinged work describes a razor-bodied fiend pulsing with flesh-searing heat as it crushed scorched bodies under massive claws. The few who have faced a diabolus and survived tend to agree with this depiction.

li.label: baby crying
li.description: That shrill wailing sound is so irritating!

li.label: my baby is crying
li.description: My baby is crying. I hope it stops soon.

li.label: baby giggling
li.description: A giggling baby just brings a smile to my face.

li.label: my baby giggling
li.description: My baby is the cutest in the anthrosphere!

li.label: killed a child
li.description: Killing one so young feels wrong, no matter the situation.

li.label: my birth mother {0} died
li.description: My birth mother died. She's gone forever. It's like a hole in my life.

li.label: my birth mother {0} lost
li.description: My birth mother has been lost. I hope she will get back to us someday.

li.label: ate baby food
li.description: I had to eat watery slop made for a child. It's not just tasteless; it's demoralizing.

li.label: fed on by {0}
li.description: I was violated by a bloodfeeder like some kind of livestock.

li.label: ingested hemogen pack
li.description: I ingested a hemogen pack. It might keep me alive, but it was absolutely disgusting.

li.label: pregnancy terminated
li.description: My pregnancy was terminated.

li.label: pregnancy terminated
li.description: My pregnancy was terminated.

li.label: pregnancy terminated
li.description: My pregnancy was terminated.

li.label: pregnancy ended
li.description: I'm relieved I'm not pregnant any more.

li.label: stillbirth
li.description: My child died during labor.

li.label: miscarried
li.description: I lost my child.

li.label: {0} miscarried
li.description: My child's story ended before it started.

li.label: {0} was born healthy
li.description: My baby brings me so much joy. I would move earth and sky for my little one.

li.label: psychic bond torn ({0})
li.description: My psychic bond with {OTHERPAWN} was torn apart. I feel like part of my mind and emotions are missing.

li.label: genes harvested
li.description: They extracted my genes like I'm some sort of lab creature.

li.label: genetic joy
li.description: Natural bonus from 'very happy' gene.

li.label: genetic optimism
li.description: Natural bonus from 'happy' gene.

li.label: genetic pessimism
li.description: Natural penalty from 'unhappy' gene.

li.label: genetic depression
li.description: Natural penalty from 'very unhappy' gene.

li.label: learning-starved
li.description: It's been so long since I learned anything new. I'm tired of the monotony!

li.label: learning-deprived
li.description: I want to learn more about all sorts of things. This place is boring!

li.label: learning unfulfilled
li.description: I need more opportunities to learn and more time to study.

li.label: learning satisfied
li.description: I've learned a lot recently! I'm looking forward to learning more.

li.label: learning fully satisfied
li.description: I've learned so much! I love all these new experiences.

li.label: desperately wants to play
li.description: Play. With. Me. Now!

li.label: really wants to play
li.description: Why won't anybody play with me?

li.label: wants to play
li.description: This place is boring.

li.label: entertained
li.description: I'm having lots of fun.

li.label: very entertained
li.description: I'm having so much fun!

li.label: pregnancy mood collapse
li.description: This pregnancy is so hard. My body always feels awful. So exhausting!

li.label: pregnancy mood down
li.description: It feels like everything is going wrong for me today. Pregnancy is tough.

li.label: pregnancy mood up
li.description: Everything feels a little bit more pleasant today. Pregnancy is nice.

li.label: pregnancy mood high
li.description: I feel amazing! Being pregnant is a gift!

li.label: kill thirst
li.description: Must kill... it has been too long since I have killed somebody up close and personal.

li.label: sunlight sensitivity
li.description: The sun hurts my eyes and my skin is tingling unpleasantly.

li.label: sunlight sensitivity
li.description: The sunlight burns my eyes and my skin feels like it's being scorched.

li.label: scanning sickness
li.description: Ever since that scan I've been dizzy and I can't think.

li.label: deathrest exhaustion
li.description: The casket calls and I fall weary. The world's pall makes all so dreary. I need to deathrest.

li.label: apocriton hatred (intense)
li.description: I feel its hatred inside me, the way I feel my own emotions. It's so close and so cold. They all deserve death.

li.label: apocriton hatred (strong)
li.description: I hear its hatred echoing between my thoughts. Reasons, always reasons why my friends ought to die.

li.label: apocriton hatred (distant)
li.description: I feel it out there somewhere. It's always thinking about why these people deserve death. Always following the logic of murder. Hard to ignore.

li.label: acidic smog
li.description: The smog makes my eyes water and it smells awful. I wish I could just have a few fresh breaths.

li.label: recluse alone
li.description: It's a relief not to have to think about other people.

li.label: recluse in small group
li.description: I'm happy I don't have too many people to think about. Alone would be better, but this is good too.

li.label: recluse crowded
li.description: There's too many people around here. The weight of having to think about them bears down on me.

li.label: recluse very crowded
li.description: There are so many people I'm supposed to be working with. They're overwhelming.

li.label: childlike joy
li.description: New! Fun! Pretty! Oooh!

li.label: childlike wonder
li.description: The world is a magical place and I can't wait to grow up!

li.label: childlike enthusiasm
li.description: The world is full of wonders.

li.label: childlike confidence
li.description: There are so many interesting things to learn.

li.label: new pregnancy
li.description: I'm pregnant! It makes me happy.

li.label: new pregnancy
li.description: I'm pregnant and not very happy about it.

li.label: psychic bond
li.description: The bond brings us together, sharing feelings and thoughts. It's like a friend who is always with me.

li.label: psychic bond distance
li.description: The distance makes it so hard to hear. I feel alone, like standing in a dark, silent cavern.

li.label: deathrested outside
li.description: I had to deathrest outdoors. It was awful.

li.label: awful deathrest chamber
li.description: I had to deathrest in an awful chamber.

li.label: decent deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in a decent chamber.

li.label: good deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in a slightly impressive chamber. It was nice.

li.label: great deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in an impressive chamber. I feel rejuvenated.

li.label: excellent deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in a very impressive chamber. I feel amazing.

li.label: exceptional deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in an extremely impressive chamber. It was glorious.

li.label: unbelievable deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in an unbelievably impressive chamber. It was spectacular.

li.label: wondrous deathrest chamber
li.description: I deathrested in such a luxurious chamber! It was wondrous.

li.label: blood torch
li.description: No flame burns as softly as a blood torch.

li.label: hemogen craving
li.description: My bones ache. I really need hemogen.

li.label: hemogen craving
li.description: This hurts bad and my head is fuzzy. I would kill for some blood. Maybe I should.

li.label: hemogen craving
li.description: Can't think. Thirst. Thirst. Must. Have. Blood.

li.label: my child {CHILD_nameDef} is happy
li.description: Nothing makes me feel better than my kid being happy.

li.label: my children are happy
li.description: Nothing makes me feel better than my kids being happy.

li.label: my child {CHILD_nameDef} is unhappy
li.description: I worry about my child. If they're not happy, I'm not happy.

li.label: my children are unhappy
li.description: I worry about my children. If they're not happy, I'm not happy.

li.label: happy youngsters
li.description: It's nice to see that the young folk are doing well.

li.label: sad youngsters
li.description: It's sad to see that the young folk are struggling.

li.label: enslaved child
li.description: It breaks my heart to see my child forced to serve others.

li.label: my baby {BABY_nameDef} is sick
li.description: My baby is sick. I'm terrified something bad will happen to my baby.

li.label: my babies are sick
li.description: My babies are sick. I'm terrified something bad will happen to them.

li.label: my child is in a growth vat
li.description: I miss my child. It's hard knowing they're floating in that machine, bypassing their childhood.

li.label: parent is happy
li.description: I'm happy when my parents are happy.

li.label: parents are happy
li.description: I'm happy when my parents are happy.

li.label: good crib
li.description: This crib is comfy.

li.label: excellent crib
li.description: This crib is very comfy.

li.label: masterwork crib
li.description: This crib is amazing. So comfortable.

li.label: legendary crib
li.description: This crib is wonderful. So very comfortable. Perfect for naps.

tips.li: Mechanitors can summon powerful mechs. Fight them yourself - or draw them into your enemies.
Children can sleep in the same room as parents and other children without any negative mood effect.
The more polluted nearby world tiles are, the more often you'll get acidic smog.
When starting a new game, you can create custom xenotypes with any genetic combination you want.
Enemies are less likely to attack children when they are unarmed. Keep kids safer by not giving them weapons.

li.label: delicate
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} has fragile skin and bones. {PAWN_pronoun} takes more damage than other people from the same blows.

li.label: recluse
li.description: The fewer people in {PAWN_nameDef}'s faction, the happier {PAWN_pronoun} is. Being alone is best of all.

ConceptDef.label: polluted terrain
ConceptDef.helpText:
Keep your colonists away from polluted terrain. Whenever they are on polluted terrain, they will continuously gain toxic buildup. This eventually becomes lethal.

Clean polluted terrain by placing a POLLUTION REMOVAL AREA. Colonists will convert the pollution into toxic wastepacks, which must be kept frozen.

Certain apparel, implants and gene modifications can protect from toxic buildup.

Normal crops cannot survive on polluted terrain.

ConceptDef.label: babies
ConceptDef.helpText:
Babies can't walk and must be taken care of. In the work tab, assign someone to childcare.

You can use the baby's 'feeding' tab to assign specific people to feed the baby. Alternatively, colonists assigned to childcare will feed babies food they can eat, such as baby food, milk, and insect jelly. You can produce baby food at a stove or campfire.

Babies can sleep in beds or cribs. A high quality crib will make a baby happy. You can also place multiple cribs in a bedroom without turning it into a barracks.

Babies become children at age 3. By default, babies age 4x faster than adults. You can adjust this in storyteller challenge settings.

ConceptDef.label: children
ConceptDef.helpText:
As they get older, children gain traits and passions, and become able to do more work types.

Children have a learning need which can be fulfilled several ways. You can see the learning activities that a child desires on their Needs tab. Children will only do learning activities when their schedule is set to Recreation or Anything. A satisfied learning need helps a child gain growth tiers faster, resulting in more passions and choices during growth moments.

Children can only wear special child-sized apparel.

Children become adults at age 13. By default, children age 4x faster than adults. You can adjust this in storyteller challenge settings.

ConceptDef.label: Deathrest
ConceptDef.helpText:
Colonists with the deathrest gene must periodically regenerate themselves in a special coma called deathrest. This takes several days.

Special machines placed near the casket can give bonuses to the deathrester. A person can only connect to a limited number of machines - this number is shown by their deathrest capacity.

You can increase deathrest capacity by injecting deathrest capacity serums. These can be purchased from traders.

ConceptDef.label: Genes and xenotypes
ConceptDef.helpText:
Some people have different genes from baseline humans. View a person's genes by opening their Bio tab and clicking the xenotype name near the top.

A xenotype is a set of genes which defines a "species" of alternate human.

There are two types of genes: Germline genes are passed on to children, while xenogenes are not and must be implanted using xenogerms.

Create custom xenotypes by researching xenogenetics and building a gene assembler.

ConceptDef.label: Mechanitors
ConceptDef.helpText:
Mechanitors use a mechlink implant to control mechanoids.

Mechanoids are assigned to control groups. You can change the behavior mode for a control group by selecting the mechanoid or mechanitor, then clicking the behavior mode icon on the control group. Gear and implants can increase the number of control groups.

Mechanitors only have the bandwidth to control a certain number of mechanoids. Special mechanitor gear and band node buildings can increase a mechanitor's total bandwidth.

The MECHS tab provides an overview of your colony's mechanoids. Here, you can draft mechanoids, change their control group, set allowed areas, and more.

Mechanitors can also summon powerful enemy super-mechanoids. These super-mechanoids drop unique chips which can be used to advance your mechanoid technology and build special units.

ConceptDef.label: Mechs in caravans
ConceptDef.helpText: While caravanning, mechanoids enter a semi-dormant long-travel state to preserve power. This allows them to travel long distances without losing energy. After arriving at their destination, mechanoids will automatically return to their previous work mode.

WorkTypeDef.description: Care for a baby or child of the colony.

ThingDef.label: reinforced concrete wall
ThingDef.description: A solid wall of concrete strengthened with embedded steel reinforcement. It is extremely durable and cannot catch fire.

ThingDef.label: thick reinforced concrete wall
ThingDef.description: An exceptionally thick wall of steel-reinforced concrete. It is built to withstand sustained bombardment and cannot catch fire.

JobDef.reportString: installing a fuse-fired breaching charge on TargetA.
installing a shock-tube breaching charge on TargetA.

ThingDef.label: installed breaching charge
ThingDef.description: C-4 fixed to a wall or door and linked to a nearby operator. Firing it immediately destroys the target structure, suppresses the far side with confined blast pressure, and drives fragments through the breach. Blast damage is limited to the target's remaining hit points, wasting any excess charge strength.

ThingDef.label: M220 TOW launcher
ThingDef.description: A crew-served tube-launched, optically tracked, wire-guided anti-tank missile launcher. Its launch tube remains in place after firing and accepts several types of TOW missile.

ThingDef.label: M167 VADS
ThingDef.description: A towed 20 mm Vulcan air defense system with a 500-round ammunition drum. Its six-barrel rotary cannon saturates exposed targets with an extremely dense burst of fire. It must be directly operated by a pawn.

ThingDef.label: vacuum induction melting furnace
ThingDef.description: A sealed induction furnace that melts metal under vacuum. Its controlled atmosphere keeps reactive gases and contaminants out, allowing exceptionally clean and precise alloy production.

HediffDef.label: CS irritation
HediffDef.description: Exposure to CS tear agent is causing painful eye, skin, and airway irritation. Symptoms fade after leaving the gas.

ThingDef.label: 20x102mm mixed ammunition
ThingDef.description: A linked 20x102mm ammunition supply for the M167 VADS, assembled in its standard mixed feed of high-explosive incendiary, high-explosive incendiary tracer, and armor-piercing incendiary projectiles.

ThingDef.label: BGM-71A missile
ThingDef.description: An early wire-guided anti-tank missile for the M220 TOW launcher.

ThingDef.label: M1952A flak jacket
ThingDef.description: A sleeveless fragmentation vest issued for protection against shell and grenade fragments. It is lighter and more flexible than modern plate armor, but offers substantially less protection against direct rifle fire.

ThingDef.label: AN-M14 TH3 incendiary grenade
ThingDef.description: Heavy thermate grenades designed to destroy equipment, weapons and vehicles with an intensely hot incendiary reaction that readily starts fires.

ThingDef.label: M7A2 CS riot-control grenade
ThingDef.description: Burning-type riot-control grenades filled with CS tear agent. The choking, eye-watering cloud incapacitates exposed targets without relying on fragmentation.

ThingDef.label: M381 40×46mm HE grenade
ThingDef.description: A 40×46mm low-velocity high-explosive grenade for the M79. It produces a broad fragmentation blast against personnel and light cover.

ThingDef.label: M433 40×46mm HEDP grenade
ThingDef.description: A dual-purpose 40×46mm grenade with a shaped-charge liner. Its smaller blast retains much better armor penetration than a standard fragmentation grenade.

ThingDef.label: M576 40×46mm multiple-projectile round
ThingDef.description: A close-range 40×46mm multiple-projectile cartridge that fires twenty pellets using standard shotgun ballistics.

ThingDef.label: M651 40×46mm CS grenade
ThingDef.description: A 40×46mm riot-control grenade that releases CS tear agent at the impact point.

ThingDef.label: 40×46mm sponge grenade
ThingDef.description: A less-lethal 40×46mm impact round with a deformable sponge nose. A damaging hit delivers heavy blunt force, intense pain, and short-lived physical suppression without an explosive blast.

DamageDef.label: sponge-round impact
DamageDef.deathMessage: {0} could not withstand the impact pain.

HediffDef.label: sponge-round impact shock
HediffDef.description: Repeated less-lethal impacts are causing intense pain, loss of coordination, and nausea. The shock fades quickly once the impacts stop.

ThingDef.label: M79 grenade launcher
ThingDef.description: A break-action single-shot grenade launcher chambered for 40×46mm low-velocity ammunition. Its ammunition is selected and loaded directly from the operator's inventory.

ThingDef.label: C-4
ThingDef.description: RDX compounded with polymer binders and plasticizers into moldable demolition blocks. It is powerful, weather-resistant, and extremely insensitive without a proper detonator.

ThingDef.label: M60 fuse igniter
ThingDef.description: A compact disposable weatherproof pull igniter for initiating time blasting fuse. Carry it together with C-4 to install a fuse-fired breaching charge. One igniter is consumed when the charge is installed.

ThingDef.label: M81 igniter
ThingDef.description: A disposable modern pull igniter capable of initiating either time blasting fuse or non-electric shock tube. Shock-tube installation takes longer, but permits the operator to move much farther from the charge before firing. One igniter is consumed when the charge is installed.

ThingDef.label: M222 missile
ThingDef.description: A 140 mm shaped-charge missile guided through a command wire by an M47 Dragon launcher.

ThingDef.label: M47 Dragon
ThingDef.description: A disposable man-portable anti-tank guided missile system. The operator must keep the target in sight while commands travel through a wire to the missile. Pulsed steering charges correct its course in visible steps, and the operator may transfer guidance to another target while the missile is in flight.

ThingDef.label: M60E3 general-purpose machine gun
ThingDef.description: A stripped-down lightweight modernization of the belt-fed M60, fitted with a forward pistol grip and improved barrel assembly but no bipod. A Helod sharpshooter can trade effective range and a little accuracy for much faster point-fire target acquisition.

ThingDef.label: power cutter
ThingDef.description: A heavy cordless cut-off saw designed to slice through masonry, metal framing, and other construction materials. Its exposed blade makes it a vicious close-combat weapon in an emergency. While equipped, it increases construction speed by 25%.

ThingDef.label: M16A1
ThingDef.description: An early lightweight 5.56 mm service rifle with full-automatic fire. A Helod sharpshooter can trade eight tiles of effective range for much faster target acquisition.

ThingDef.label: M16A2
ThingDef.description: A refined 5.56 mm service rifle with improved sights, heavier furniture, and a controlled three-round burst. A Helod sharpshooter can trade eight tiles of effective range for much faster target acquisition.

ThingDef.label: M16A3
ThingDef.description: A full-automatic derivative of the M16A2 intended for sustained close-to-medium-range fire. A Helod sharpshooter can trade eight tiles of effective range for much faster target acquisition.

JobDef.reportString: breaching TargetA with a power cutter.

RecipeDef.label: compound C-4
RecipeDef.description: Blend RDX with polymer binders and plasticizers, then press the pliable explosive into sealed demolition blocks.

FactionDef.label: Helod colony
FactionDef.description: A colony of Helod pioneers building a frontier industrial outpost.

FactionDef.label: Helod Mercantile Association
FactionDef.description: Independent Helod frontier settlements bound together by trade, kinship, and practical cooperation.

FactionDef.label: 베세니카 주
FactionDef.description: A centralized Helod state whose authority extends beyond the frontier.

ThingDef.label: sthaler banknote
ThingDef.description: A beautifully engraved paper banknote used as the standard currency among Helod settlements. Known as Sthaler, it carries significant value but is highly fragile and will dissolve quickly if left unroofed in the rain.

ThingDef.label: government bond
ThingDef.description: An official, beautifully engraved paper government bond certificate issued by the United States of Vesenica. It serves as high-value, secure sovereign wealth storage. It cannot be stacked and must be handled with care.

ThingDef.label: Continental Petroleum bond
ThingDef.description: An official corporate debt certificate issued by the Continental Petroleum Company, representing a face value of 100 Sthaler. Unlike sovereign government bonds, this corporate security is tied directly to the performance of the oil industry. It serves as highly liquid industrial wealth storage.

ThingDef.label: LANCE LRA-7
ThingDef.description: A second-generation LANCE rifle using a single-measurement system to couple its positive- and negative-mass projectiles. The coupled shot gains destructive energy over distance; beyond its safe separation envelope it collapses into a feedback runaway.

Helodrace.HelodGasDef.label: photochlorogen gas
Helodrace.HelodGasDef.description: A pale delayed-action choking agent cloud. Photochlorogen first irritates the airways, then may seem to fade during a latent period before pulmonary edema begins damaging the lungs. Gas masks and other tox-gas exposure immunity block it.

Helodrace.HelodGasDef.label: sweet gas
Helodrace.HelodGasDef.description: A yellow delayed blister agent cloud. Sweet gas dose does not naturally fall; if no dose change occurs for several hours, the exposure is considered cleared. Gas masks and tox-gas exposure immunity do not block it; if Odyssey is installed, vacuum resistance reduces exposure.

Helodrace.HelodGasDef.label: CS gas
Helodrace.HelodGasDef.description: A dense tear-agent cloud that causes immediate eye, skin, and respiratory irritation. Gas protection and toxic-environment resistance reduce exposure.

Helodrace.HelodGasDef.label: CN gas
Helodrace.HelodGasDef.description: A persistent tear-agent cloud that develops more slowly than CS. Heavy exposure causes severe eye, skin, and respiratory irritation and may inflict minor tissue damage. Gas protection and toxic-environment resistance reduce exposure.

Helodrace.HelodGasDef.label: white phosphorus smoke
Helodrace.HelodGasDef.description: A dense, persistent cloud produced by burning white phosphorus. It obscures gunfire as effectively as an ordinary smoke screen and can ignite flammable things caught inside.

ThingDef.label: M1917 heavy machine gun
ThingDef.description: A tripod-mounted, water-cooled heavy machine gun with a 250-round belt. It must be directly operated by a pawn.

ThingDef.label: M2HB heavy machine gun
ThingDef.description: A pedestal-mounted .50 caliber heavy machine gun fed from a 100-round belt. Its powerful rounds are effective against personnel, light cover, and lightly armored targets. It must be directly operated by a pawn.

ThingDef.label: M1916 37mm gun
ThingDef.description: A crew-served 37mm direct-fire infantry gun. Its low mount is treated as a transparent base, leaving the gun itself as the visible turret top.

ThingDef.label: 3-inch Hawkins mortar
ThingDef.description: A crew-served 3-inch trench mortar for lobbing high-explosive shells over cover. It must be directly operated by a pawn and reloaded with prepared HE shells.

ThingDef.label: M1 81mm mortar
ThingDef.description: A crew-served 81mm infantry mortar for dropping M43 high-explosive shells over cover. It must be directly operated by a pawn and reloaded with prepared 81mm ammunition.

ThingDef.label: M2A2 105mm light howitzer
ThingDef.description: A 105mm field howitzer on a split-trail carriage. Its chief of section, gunner, and assistant gunner occupy separate crew positions and each contributes to accuracy, loading speed, or aiming speed. All required roles must be staffed before it can fire. It accepts dedicated M1 105mm HE shells as well as standard mortar shells.

ThingDef.label: M114 155mm howitzer
ThingDef.description: A medium 155mm field howitzer on a split-trail carriage. Its section chief, gunner, and assistant gunner must all be at their stations before it can fire, while additional crew improve aiming and loading. It uses dedicated 155mm high-explosive, BA and CN chemical, white-phosphorus, and W48 nuclear shells for long-range indirect fire.

ThingDef.label: ANFO blasting charge
ThingDef.description: A prepared ammonium nitrate and diesel blasting charge. It can be fired remotely by a friendly blasting detonator within 50 cells, penetrates three layers into solid rock without leaving diagonal gaps, and recovers destroyed resource veins at the yield of a level 12 miner. Direct rain exposure prevents accidental cook-off and permanently disables the charge after an average of one hour. When dry, it may cook off if badly damaged.

ThingDef.label: blasting detonator
ThingDef.description: A hand-operated blasting machine wired to every friendly ANFO charge within 50 cells. Select it and use the detonation command to fire all connected charges at once.

ThingDef.label: high-pressure reactor
ThingDef.description: A reinforced catalytic reactor that fixes atmospheric nitrogen under extreme pressure. Supplied with a hydrogen-rich fuel feed, it produces ammonium nitrate for fertilizer and explosives.

ThingDef.label: stirred-tank reactor
ThingDef.description: An electrically driven, jacketed reaction vessel for controlled nitration and other liquid-phase chemistry. Its sealed agitator keeps volatile reagents thoroughly mixed while carrying away reaction heat.

RecipeDef.label: synthesize ammonium nitrate
RecipeDef.description: Fix atmospheric nitrogen with a hydrogen-rich chemfuel feed, then oxidize and neutralize the resulting ammonia to produce ammonium nitrate.

RecipeDef.label: synthesize TNT
RecipeDef.description: Nitrate the toluene-rich fraction of aromatic base oil in a stirred-tank reactor, then wash and cast the resulting TNT into demolition blocks.

RecipeDef.label: synthesize RDX
RecipeDef.description: Nitrate a formaldehyde-rich petrochemical feed under tightly controlled conditions, then stabilize and dry the resulting RDX crystals.

HediffDef.label: CN irritation
HediffDef.description: Exposure to CN tear agent is gradually causing painful eye, skin, and airway irritation. Severe accumulated exposure can cause minor tissue damage. Symptoms fade slowly after leaving the gas.

HediffDef.label: burning gel
HediffDef.description: Sticky incendiary gel coats this creature. Until the gel burns away, it repeatedly catches fire even after the flames are extinguished.

ThingDef.label: M2 flamethrower
ThingDef.description: A backpack-fed flamethrower that launches globs of sticky incendiary gel. Each glob scatters fire around its impact point, while a direct hit coats the victim in gel that repeatedly reignites for a short time.

HediffDef.label: plasma transfusion
HediffDef.description: Recently received an emergency plasma transfusion from a field medic bag.

ThingDef.label: M8 HC smoke grenade
ThingDef.description: Metal canister grenades that burn a hexachloroethane mixture to rapidly create a thick white screening cloud.

ThingDef.label: M15 white phosphorus grenade
ThingDef.description: White phosphorus grenades that burst into burning material while producing a dense smoke screen. They are dangerous to exposed personnel and readily ignite the surroundings.

ThingDef.label: MK II fragmentation grenade
ThingDef.description: A cast-iron defensive grenade whose deeply grooved body bursts into deadly fragments. It is heavier and less powerful than later fragmentation grenades, but remains effective against exposed infantry.

ThingDef.label: MK III offensive grenade
ThingDef.description: An offensive grenade with a thick fiberboard body packed with high explosive. It produces little dangerous fragmentation and incapacitates through powerful blast overpressure, making it especially lethal in confined spaces.

ThingDef.label: FLAM
ThingDef.description: A suspiciously long-lasting block of canned meat. FLAM is salty, filling, and compact enough to stockpile in truly unreasonable quantities.

ThingDef.label: hardtack
ThingDef.description: A dense, dry ration baked from preserved vegetarian ingredients. It keeps indefinitely, can be cooked in bulk, and is hard enough to throw in desperation.

ThingDef.label: medic bag
ThingDef.description: A basic shoulder-slung treatment bag stocked with simple herbal remedies and bandaging supplies.

ThingDef.label: M1 mortar barrel
ThingDef.description: The barrel and breech assembly of an M1 81mm mortar, fitted with carrying straps. It is one of the three heavy loads into which the weapon is broken down for transport.

ThingDef.label: M1 mortar baseplate
ThingDef.description: The steel baseplate of an M1 81mm mortar, rigged as a heavy back load. It spreads the weapon's recoil into the ground when the mortar is assembled.

ThingDef.label: M1 mortar bipod
ThingDef.description: The bipod mount, elevation screw, and traversing mechanism of an M1 81mm mortar, bundled for carriage. It supports and aims the barrel when assembled.

ThingDef.label: gas mask pouch
ThingDef.description: A compact belt pouch carrying a gas mask, sealed filter spares, and anti-gas cloth. Wearing the pouch makes the mask available; deploy the mask to gain full toxic environment resistance.

ThingDef.label: CBRN protection pouch
ThingDef.description: A reinforced gas mask pouch carrying sealed filters, barrier cloth, and emergency chemical-protection supplies. Wearing the pouch makes the mask available; deploy the mask to gain full toxic environment resistance and block sweet gas exposure.

ThingDef.label: weapon system test harness
ThingDef.description: An experimental loadout-control harness. When worn, it lets a colonist configure desired inventory amounts for ammunition and automatically collect those supplies.

ThingDef.label: great war trench uniform liner
ThingDef.description: A fitted inner uniform for trench troops, tailored for Helod bodies. It is worn close to the body beneath armor or heavier field gear.

ThingDef.label: great war trench armor coat
ThingDef.description: A reinforced outer uniform for trench troops, tailored for Helod bodies. It is worn over inner clothing as protective armor and field gear.

ThingDef.label: great war storm-front uniform liner
ThingDef.description: A fitted inner uniform issued to storm-front troops, tailored for Helod bodies. It is worn close to the body beneath armor or heavier field gear.

ThingDef.label: great war storm-front uniform outer layer
ThingDef.description: A reinforced storm-front field uniform tailored for Helod bodies. It is worn over the uniform liner and beneath heavier armor and field gear.

ThingDef.label: great war storm-front chest rig
ThingDef.description: A webbing chest rig issued to storm-front infantry. Its reinforced straps and ammunition pouches keep essential field equipment secure and close at hand.

ThingDef.label: 3-inch mortar HE shell
ThingDef.description: A high-explosive bomb for the 3-inch Hawkins mortar. It is packed for indirect fire against clustered infantry and light fieldworks.

ThingDef.label: M1 105mm HE shell
ThingDef.description: A cased M1 high-explosive shell for the M2A2 105mm light howitzer. Its heavy bursting charge is intended for entrenched infantry, fortifications, and field targets.

ThingDef.label: M107 155mm HE shell
ThingDef.description: A heavy M107 high-explosive shell for the M114 155mm howitzer. Its large bursting charge devastates entrenched infantry, fortifications, and structures over a broad area.

ThingDef.label: M110 155mm BA chemical shell
ThingDef.description: An M110 chemical shell for the M114 155mm howitzer, filled with persistent HD blister agent. Its burster spreads a dense cloud of sweet gas over a wide impact area.

ThingDef.label: M110 155mm WP smoke shell
ThingDef.description: A white-phosphorus smoke shell for the M114 155mm howitzer. It lays down a broad, dense smoke screen and scatters burning phosphorus around the impact area.

ThingDef.label: M110 155mm CN chemical shell
ThingDef.description: An M110 chemical shell for the M114 155mm howitzer filled with CN tear agent. It produces a broad, persistent irritant cloud that acts more slowly than CS but becomes harmful at severe exposure.

ThingDef.label: W48 155mm nuclear shell
ThingDef.description: A compact nuclear artillery shell for the M114 155mm howitzer. Its detonation produces a devastating blast, intense fires, a powerful electromagnetic pulse, and severe pollution around ground zero. It cannot be manufactured.

ThingDef.label: M43 81mm HE shell
ThingDef.description: A fin-stabilized high-explosive shell for the M1 81mm mortar. Its heavier bursting charge is well suited to suppressing clustered infantry, fieldworks, and light structures.

ThingDef.label: M57 81mm WP smoke shell
ThingDef.description: A white-phosphorus smoke shell for the M1 81mm mortar. It creates a broad smoke screen and scatters burning phosphorus around the impact.

ThingDef.label: M57 81mm BA chemical shell
ThingDef.description: A chemical shell for the M1 81mm mortar. Its small bursting charge spreads a concentrated cloud of sweet gas over the impact area.

ThingDef.label: 37mm HE shell
ThingDef.description: A compact high-explosive shell for the M1916 37mm gun. It is built for direct fire against infantry, light cover, and exposed fieldworks.

ThingDef.label: 37mm AP shell
ThingDef.description: A solid armor-piercing shell for the M1916 37mm gun. It trades explosive blast for a hardened shot capable of punching through armor and tough targets.

ThingDef.label: M6A3 HEAT rocket
ThingDef.description: A shaped-charge rocket for the M9A1 launcher. It must be loaded before firing and is consumed when the launcher is fired.

ThingDef.label: M10 WP rocket
ThingDef.description: A white phosphorus rocket for the M9A1 launcher. It bursts with a small charge, throws up dense smoke, and scatters burning phosphorus around the impact point.

ThingDef.label: 3-inch mortar photochlorogen shell
ThingDef.description: A chemical bomb for the 3-inch Hawkins mortar. On impact it bursts once and releases a compact photochlorogen cloud, much narrower than a deployed canister.

ThingDef.label: m1 Helmet
ThingDef.description: m1 helmet with hole for ears

ThingDef.label: burning signal flare
ThingDef.description: A bright M8 signal flare marking this position. It can be selected as a target by systems that support flare designation.

ThingDef.label: M8 flare gun
ThingDef.description: A single-shot break-action signal pistol. Its burning flare remains on the map as a selectable designation marker for future close air support systems.

ThingDef.label: ammonium nitrate
ThingDef.description: A white crystalline nitrogen compound synthesized under high pressure. It is a powerful oxidizer used in fertilizer and as a precursor for industrial explosives. It is insensitive to bullets and fire, but a sufficiently powerful explosion can detonate it.

ThingDef.label: TNT
ThingDef.description: Trinitrotoluene cast into compact demolition blocks. It is insensitive to bullets and fire during transport, but a sufficiently powerful explosion can detonate it.

ThingDef.label: RDX
ThingDef.description: Crystalline cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine packed into sealed drums. More powerful than TNT and stable enough for transport, RDX is the principal explosive ingredient used to manufacture plastic explosives.

ThingDef.label: SCR-300 backpack radio
ThingDef.description: A rugged backpack VHF radio for direct communication with a contracted forward base. A wearer can bind the set to a forward base and request any contracted service that can reach the wearer's current map.

ThingDef.label: wooden baseball bat
ThingDef.description: A carefully shaped wooden bat made for baseball. Its balance makes it quick to swing, and its heavy barrel makes it an effective improvised weapon.

ThingDef.label: metal baseball bat
ThingDef.description: A hollow metal baseball bat with a wrapped grip. It is slightly heavier and hits harder than its wooden counterpart without becoming unwieldy.

ThingDef.label: M1916 37mm gun
ThingDef.description: A light infantry gun firing compact explosive shells in direct fire. It needs a crew and prepared 37mm ammunition.

ThingDef.label: Ironfang M1911
ThingDef.description: Hartmann's masterpiece, a gun handed down from grandfathers, and a gun like the heart of Vessenica. A rugged semi-automatic service pistol with a heavy cartridge and fast follow-up shots.

ThingDef.label: M1A1 Harrington
ThingDef.description: A rugged submachine gun with a heavy bolt and a fast cyclic rate. It fires hard-hitting pistol cartridges in controlled bursts.

ThingDef.label: M3A1 submachine gun
ThingDef.description: A compact stamped-metal submachine gun built for simple production and steady close-range automatic fire.

ThingDef.label: M9A1 recoilless launcher
ThingDef.description: A shoulder-fired recoilless rocket launcher for attacking armor, emplacements, and clustered hard targets. It must be loaded before firing, can be operated alone or by a two-pawn crew, and fires a shaped-charge M6A3 HEAT rocket in a flat, visible line.

ThingDef.label: M1917 heavy machine gun
ThingDef.description: A water-cooled heavy machine gun fed by a long ammunition belt. It is too heavy to use as a carried weapon and is intended for fixed defensive mounts.

ThingDef.label: M2HB heavy machine gun
ThingDef.description: A belt-fed .50 caliber heavy machine gun intended for fixed defensive mounts.

ThingDef.label: 3-inch Hawkins mortar
ThingDef.description: A simple infantry mortar firing high-explosive bombs in a high arc. It requires a crew and prepared shells.

ThingDef.label: M1 81mm mortar
ThingDef.description: A battalion infantry mortar firing heavy 81mm bombs in a high arc. It requires a crew and prepared M43 HE shells.

ThingDef.label: M2A2 105mm light howitzer
ThingDef.description: A 105mm field howitzer configured for long-range indirect fire with dedicated M1 high-explosive shells or standard mortar shells.

ThingDef.label: Graylock M1892
ThingDef.description: A Graylock Arsenal production of the Berg-Larsen rifle, a bolt-action design with a unique side-loading magazine. Famous for its smooth action.

ThingDef.label: Frontier Arms M1897
ThingDef.description: A rugged pump-action trench shotgun built for close fighting. Its tubular magazine and fast action make it devastating at short range.

ThingDef.label: M1A1 carbine
ThingDef.description: A compact, lightweight semi-automatic carbine fitted with a folding wire stock. It is quick to shoulder and easy to carry, trading the power and reach of a full-size service rifle for excellent handling.

ThingDef.label: M2 carbine
ThingDef.description: A select-fire development of the lightweight service carbine. Its controllable cartridge and compact frame make it effective in close fighting, though sustained automatic fire quickly loses precision at range.

ThingDef.label: M1 Hartwell
ThingDef.description: A semi-automatic battle rifle fed by an en-bloc clip. It gives up a little deliberate precision for rapid, powerful follow-up fire. In later stories, the adoption of small-caliber high-velocity rounds was delayed by the Dark Hartwell Order.

ThingDef.label: M1D Hartwell
ThingDef.description: A scoped M1 Hartwell variant built for accurate semi-automatic fire at extended range. It trades some close handling for steadier long-range shooting.

ThingDef.label: M1918A2 HAR
ThingDef.description: A heavy automatic rifle designed to walk with the infantry line. Its slow-fire setting keeps short bursts controllable, while sharpshooters can brace into a faster suppressive mode.

ThingDef.label: M1919A6 light machine gun
ThingDef.description: A portable belt-fed machine gun adapted from the Hartmann M1919. Heavy for an infantry weapon, but able to lay down sustained suppressive fire.

ThingDef.label: Graylock M1903
ThingDef.description: A reliable and accurate bolt-action rifle that served for decades. Highly prized for its precision.

ThingDef.label: Graylock M1903A4
ThingDef.description: A scoped M1903 variant prepared for deliberate long-range fire. It keeps the familiar action of the service rifle while stretching its effective reach.

ThingDef.label: Graylock M1903 Whitmore device
ThingDef.description: An M1903 rifle fitted with a Whitmore conversion device. It uses lighter ammunition instead of full-power rifle cartridges, allowing fast semi-automatic fire.

ThingDef.label: M1902 officer saber
ThingDef.description: A light ceremonial service saber carried by officers. It looks proper on parade, but its narrow blade and light fittings make it a poor battlefield weapon.

ThingDef.label: KA-BUG USMC fighting knife
ThingDef.description: A sturdy clip-point combat knife worn at the waist for fighting and field utility. While equipped, it adds quick knife thrusts and cuts to the wearer's available melee attacks.

ThingDef.label: M114 155mm howitzer
ThingDef.description: A medium field howitzer configured for deliberate long-range indirect fire with dedicated 155mm high-explosive, BA and CN chemical, white-phosphorus, and W48 nuclear shells.

JobDef.reportString: loading treatment supplies into medic bag.
standing by as recoilless weapon loader.
moving to the M1 mortar assembly site.
reloading M79 grenade launcher from inventory.

ThingDef.label: photochlorogen can
ThingDef.description: A small chemical canister rigged with an ignition cap. When activated, it burns open and spreads photochlorogen gas across a wide nearby area. Gas masks and other tox-gas exposure immunity block the gas.

HediffDef.label: photochlorogen dose
HediffDef.description: Photochlorogen has entered the body. A higher dose accelerates the delayed risk of respiratory injury, even if symptoms fade for a while after exposure. Medical treatment can help clear the dose faster, with better treatment quality removing more.

HediffDef.label: photochlorogen injury risk
HediffDef.description: Delayed respiratory injury from photochlorogen exposure. Early reaction-phase symptoms can recover naturally after the dose fades, but once the condition reaches the latent phase it no longer naturally recovers and will continue progressing at least slowly. The risk requires repeated treatment every hour; each treatment greatly slows progression for three hours, and a total of 500% treatment quality clears it before pulmonary edema becomes fatal.

RaidStrategyDef.arrivalTextEnemy: The raiders are establishing a field position with an M1 mortar, automatic-rifle cover, ammunition, and rations.
The raiders are attacking as a breaching team. Most carry submachine guns in sharpshooter mode, supported by one or two snipers and a two-pawn M9A1 recoilless-launcher crew.

The raiders intend to make a show of force around the colony. They will patrol the perimeter, fire on colonists they can see, and attempt to carry away anyone they down instead of launching a direct assault.
The raiders are establishing a protected field position with an M1 mortar and BA chemical shells. Every member is carrying CBRN protection.

RecipeDef.label: make FLAM x20
RecipeDef.description: Can a large batch of finely processed meat into compact tins of FLAM.

RecipeDef.label: make hardtack x32
RecipeDef.description: Bake a bulk batch of long-lasting hardtack from vegetarian ingredients.

RecipeDef.label: make 3-inch mortar HE shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a high-explosive shell for the 3-inch Hawkins mortar.

RecipeDef.label: make M43 81mm HE shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a high-explosive M43 shell for the M1 81mm mortar.

RecipeDef.label: make M1 105mm HE shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a cased M1 high-explosive shell for the M2A2 105mm light howitzer.

RecipeDef.label: make M107 155mm HE shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a heavy M107 high-explosive shell for the M114 155mm howitzer.

RecipeDef.label: make M110 155mm BA chemical shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble an M110 chemical shell filled with persistent HD blister agent for the M114 155mm howitzer.

RecipeDef.label: make M110 155mm WP smoke shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a white-phosphorus smoke shell for the M114 155mm howitzer.

RecipeDef.label: make M110 155mm CN chemical shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble an M110 CN tear-agent shell for the M114 155mm howitzer.

RecipeDef.label: make M57 81mm WP smoke shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a white-phosphorus smoke shell for the M1 81mm mortar.

RecipeDef.label: make M57 81mm BA chemical shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a sweet-gas chemical shell for the M1 81mm mortar.

RecipeDef.label: make 37mm HE shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a compact high-explosive shell for the M1916 37mm gun.

RecipeDef.label: make 37mm AP shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a hardened armor-piercing shell for the M1916 37mm gun.

RecipeDef.label: make M6A3 HEAT rocket
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a shaped-charge rocket for the M9A1 recoilless launcher.

RecipeDef.label: make M10 WP rocket
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a white phosphorus smoke rocket for the M9A1 recoilless launcher.

RecipeDef.label: make 3-inch mortar photochlorogen shell
RecipeDef.description: Assemble a compact photochlorogen shell for the 3-inch Hawkins mortar.

ThingDef.label: sweet gas can
ThingDef.description: A temporary chemical canister using the photochlorogen can body. When activated, it burns open and releases sweet gas, a delayed blister agent. Gas masks and tox-gas exposure immunity do not block the gas; if Odyssey is installed, vacuum resistance reduces exposure.

HediffDef.label: sweet gas dose
HediffDef.description: Sweet gas has entered the body. This dose does not naturally decrease; if the dose remains unchanged for several hours, the body clears the exposure state. Medical treatment can reduce the dose faster, with better treatment quality removing more.

HediffDef.label: sweet gas injury risk
HediffDef.description: Delayed blister-agent injury from sweet gas exposure. The latent phase has no symptoms. Once the active phase begins, sweet gas causes extreme pain and periodically adds severe permanent scars to three random external body parts that are not already scarred by it. Late active exposure has a high chance to kill. Treatment slows progression for three hours, and a total of 500% treatment quality clears the risk.

TerrainDef.label: fertile earth
TerrainDef.description: Earth enriched with ammonium nitrate. It can only be laid over growable soil, and crops grow considerably faster in it.

BackstoryDef.title: pipeline pup
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up around frontier pump camps, carrying tools, counting barrels, and learning to sleep through the thump of machinery.

BackstoryDef.title: telegraph runner
BackstoryDef.description: As a young courier, [PAWN_nameDef] carried coded slips between banks, rail camps, and lonely telegraph offices on the edge of settled space.

BackstoryDef.title: foundry orphan
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was raised by a smoky machine yard where spare hands were expected to sort coal, fetch water, and keep clear of red-hot iron.

BackstoryDef.title: frontier mechanic
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] kept battered engines, pumps, and line shafts alive with improvised parts and stubborn patience. The frontier rarely offered a second chance for bad repairs.

BackstoryDef.title: oil claim guard
BackstoryDef.description: Hired to protect surveyors and oil claims, [PAWN_nameDef] learned to read dust, distance, and the twitch of a hand near a holster.

BackstoryDef.title: Sthaler clerk
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] balanced ledgers for a frontier finance house, turning ore, oil, debts, and favors into neat columns of money.

BackstoryDef.title: prairie doctor
